COLLECTOR'S NOTE: items marked 'collector observation' are tensions this read-only pass noticed. They are not rulings and should be verified.

items.finding: FMT model definition changed. MG, verbatim: 'definition of model should say it is readable, not that it is actually read. that is only required for actual consciousness'. Master §3.1 now reads: 'T fixes the model's boundary; updating M so that it follows T is the write access of Table 1, and the capacity to evaluate it is the read access. A model must be readable; that it is actually read is required only for consciousness (Section 3.4.3). A structure the system cannot evaluate is a data structure, not a model.' Table 1 'Model' now has two criteria: (1) write access (updates from new input) and (2) read access ('its representations can be evaluated by the system; being read is required only for consciousness'). Write access is no longer defined through an evaluation error (AIW-363 edit E1).
items.source: docs/decisions.md:819 (D-S366-A); master four-model-theory-full.md §3.1 l.152 and Table 1 l.164; commit a7d1a39b; crucible docs/decisions.md 2026-10-30 entries (~08:50 and 'via aIware S366')
items.bears_on: Model definition. The formalization never defines 'model'. §2.1 calls each point of M 'a distinct model the substrate is running', and §4.1 treats the explicit models as projections Π·x(t). Neither states the write/readable criteria or that being read is a consciousness condition, not a model condition. Also bears on §6.4: closure and consciousness presuppose actual reading, model status does not.
items.scope_limits: Applied to master md + tex in S366 but not yet deposited (awaits MG review). It refines crucible's earlier relay (~09:10: WRITE confirmed, READ not required to claim explicit models).

items.finding: Boundary recognition is demoted from a third model criterion to a consequence of the target domain. Table 1 now reads: 'Boundary recognition (differential response inside vs. outside the target domain; Gruber, 2015) follows from the target domain, which fixes the model's boundary.' MG had chosen 'Write is enough' for the crucible instrument (~08:53) and asked 'how is read access different from readable?'. Answer recorded: they are identical since D-S366-A; the distinction that matters is readable vs actually read.
items.source: docs/decisions.md:825 (D-S366-G, T7); master Table 1 l.164; crucible docs/decisions.md 2026-10-30 ~08:50 ('Boundary: MG chose Write is enough')
items.bears_on: Model definition; the explicit/implicit threshold (§4.6 characterizes ν_crit by graph structure, not by model criteria); §2.6 criteria for real modes versus artifacts.

items.finding: Operational model criteria and world-model parts, MG in the crucible console. ~08:50, verbatim: 'write criterion is correct, read criterion is evidence for consciousness by fmt, not required for just saying there are explicit models, generated not stored is a very trivial thing'. D19 (~14:46), verbatim: 'i already told you that all explicit models that are not the self model are world model parts'. Applied: an explicit model = recurring activity that passes WRITE for some target and is readable. 'Arbitrary directions of the activity are not models.' Closure = mutual updating between the self model and explicit models outside it that themselves pass WRITE.
items.bears_on: §4.1 (EWM(t) = Π_EWM·x(t), ESM(t) = Π_ESM·x(t)): a projection/direction of x(t) is a model only if it follows a target and is readable. §2.2/§2.6 estimation of ρ by ICA/NMF/RSA: components need a target test. §6.4: the w entering Ψ must consist of WRITE-passing models, not arbitrary activity.
items.scope_limits: Given in crucible's operational context. D19 came after aIware's S366 record and is not in aIware docs/decisions.md. The theory content matches D-S366-D (3).

items.finding: Persistence criterion loosened. MG, verbatim (a ruling, not a hedge): 'the pattern need not occur in consecutive windows strictly, it may re-occur every n steps.' A pattern that recurs after gaps counts as the same object. The S366 framework restates a model as 'recurring activity'.
items.bears_on: What an explicit model is as activity: persistence vs recurrence. It bears on any formal object assuming continuous persistence (ρ(s,ν,t) as a continuous-time density; the attractor framing of §5.1). It also bears on Principle 2's 'persistent activity patterns that survive their own inputs' (T5, F16).
items.scope_limits: Crucible instrument context. The master's Principle 2 wording is not yet changed (T5 pending CRU-238).

items.finding: Explicit models are ACTIVITY, never regions. MG, verbatim: 'building four substrate based models is BS in terms of FMT. FMT requires two substrate level models, the implicit ones. The explicit models ARE sustained spiking patterns, that are robust, besides more flexible/dynamical spiking patterns. the explicit models MUST EMERGER FROM implicit models AS ACTIVITY given the correct connectome form and weights ... Explicit models ARE NOT REGIONS IN A NETWORK, that would be a total misunderstanding of FMT.' Robust patterns correspond to 'what the body does and sees'; dynamical ones are 'active, prospective planning and modeling/simulating for future'. Correction ~23:00: the body model is not one area or column; it 'uses a good fraction of the total cortex area'. Core principle: 'the secret is in defining, finding and analyzing spiking activita AS MODELS, thats the trick FMT offers'. The RCA notes that the formalization 'does invite [the region reading] by its wording': fmt-formalization.md:41 ('four *regions* in a continuous space of modeling activity') and :92 ('four regions R_IWM … R_ESM'). Those are regions of an abstract scope/mode space, 'but it is the same word'.
items.source: docs/sources/mg-2026-10-27-fmt-substrate-spec.md; docs/research/fmt-crucible-misread-rca.md §2 ('Do the aIware texts invite the region reading?'); ~/crucible/docs/decisions.md 2026-10-27 ~22:45/23:00 (l.447+); D-S365-B (decisions.md:818)
items.bears_on: Wording in §1.2 l.41 and §2.3 (R_IWM … R_ESM 'regions'). §4.1 projection operators (must not be read as cell masks). §4.6 says explicit processing is 'low-dimensional, structured, and local', which can be read as localization (cf. registry misreading #5). §5.2 'DMN activity (proxy for ESM)'. §8 Module 4 'Build a minimal computational model with a self-model unit' (a module). §2.7 engine localization as a 'region'. The robust/dynamical distinction is a dimension the scope × mode (× ℓ) model space does not have. The continuous mode axis ν sits beside a ruling that there are two kinds, stored structure (W) and activity.
items.scope_limits: Given about crucible's build after the Jülich explainer. The theory statement is unhedged. MG: a four-region network is 'not impossible — no free lunch — but not FMT'.

items.finding: Input-locked patterns count as explicit models, and 'robust vs dynamical' is a KIND question, not a model criterion. D-S366-C (MG, hedged 'i'd say probably yes'): a pattern that only re-carries its input area's signal probably counts as a simple robust explicit model; beating an input filter is a KIND question (robust vs dynamical), not a model criterion. Resolved by D-S366-E (MG chose 'Explicit self-model now'). crucible fmt-core: 'robust = locked to current input, lives only while the input lasts. Dynamical = carries future or absent states, internal onset. A model need not beat a filter of its input'.
items.bears_on: The explicit/implicit threshold ν_crit: explicit includes input-locked robust activity, so 'explicit' cannot be defined by independence from input. §4.6 graph phase-transition characterization. Model-space dimensionality (robust/dynamical kind). aIware D-S366-C: any text treating input-locked patterns as non-models must be checked.
items.scope_limits: D7 was provisional; D10 settled it for crucible's frontal direction. The general kind distinction comes from MG's 2026-10-27 spec plus crucible's merged definition.

items.finding: First simple explicit self model, without closure. A free-frontal weighted area-rate direction is 'an integrated, lower-dimensional model of hunger + pain + danger proximity' in 3/3 creatures (8k cells, learning off), 'without closure (no active world or self model)'. Same day, crucible results: sensory-near world-model parts exist (the visual area follows food and danger position, 8k 3/3, 40k 2/2). No closure was found between the self model and the world-model parts beyond arbitrary directions (8k 0/3, 40k 0/2).
items.bears_on: §2.3 minimum-configuration constraint: ESM mass can exist with no closure. §3.5 χ_loop: ESM content outside the loop. §8 Phase 4 computational validation. The §6.3 levels table (no closure means below minimal consciousness).
items.scope_limits: Toy spiking creature, frozen weights, a single relayed-signal pattern (the frontal direction adds ~0 beyond the insula: R² 0.62–0.77 vs 0.83–0.87). Not a consciousness claim. Must-not-say rules unchanged. CRU-238 (input cut) pending.

items.finding: The realistic ESM is a lower-dimensional, integrated MODEL of the actual self ('copy' withdrawn). MG, verbatim (T8): 'they are generated by the substrate: correct. they are integrated from several implicit models plus sensory input plus motor feedback etc. as needed for the entity, modulated by salience and memory etc etc. the simplest possible self model would be a low dimensional model (not "copy") of the body or at least a viewpoint projected into the real world from which the senses seem to get their information.' Earlier MG: 'only complexer tasks and worlds and selves can start to show a strong difference between explicit and implicit models'. Master §3.2 now says the ESM 'departs strongly from the implicit self models only in imagination, as in imagining being a horse or a chair. Only complex tasks, worlds and selves show a strong difference between explicit and implicit models; in a simple system the two are hard to tell apart.'
items.bears_on: §5.1 e(t) as the aggregate ESM state (low-dimensional, integrated; salience modulation). §2.1 ESM corner (s≈0, ν=1). §2.2/§4.6 sharp ontological ν_crit versus 'in a simple system the two are hard to tell apart' (an epistemic/measurement limit that bears on estimating ν_crit). §6.2 O_ESM.
items.scope_limits: Undeposited master edit. The 'generated … rather than filled by a copy' sentences (l.178/417) stay; 'copy' is retired only for the ESM-to-actual-self relation.

items.finding: Minimal self model, and viewpoint ≠ position estimate. Master §3.4.3 now reads: 'a realistic representation of the organism — its states and, where it has them, its geometry and capabilities … The simplest self model is a low-dimensional, integrated model of the body, or at least a viewpoint projected into the world from which the senses seem to take their information. A position estimate alone is not one. … A viewpoint differs from a position estimate: it is the origin to which the senses are referred and which binds their input, not a coordinate on a map.' The SLAM exclusion stays.
items.bears_on: What counts as self-scope mass at s≈0 (§2.1, §2.3 θ_ESM). The self-scope content entering §6.2 O_ESM and §6.4 e. Any formal criterion separating a self model from a position datum.
items.scope_limits: Undeposited master edit.

items.finding: Nesting (ESM ⊆ EWM) is kept as the normal mode, with exceptions. MG, verbatim: 'the nesting is the normal mode of operation unless you have an out of body experience without body, like on a strong salvinorin dose with nothing for the body model to latch onto maybe, or the self model system being overwhelmed or damaged or sth. maybe cotard does sth like that also. but nested doesnt necessarily mean physically at the same neurla locations at the same time. nested is just saying that a conscious entity usually models itself within the world model, not somewhere else'. Master §3.2 adds: 'Nesting is the normal mode of operation … It can fail when the self model has nothing to latch onto or is overwhelmed or damaged, perhaps in disembodied ego dissolution under salvinorin A or in Cotard's delusion (Section 6.1). The part of the EWM outside the ESM, all explicit modeling of what is not the self, is the world model with which the self model closes.' ISM ⊆ IWM is 2015-native (Emergenz p.266 Lulu: 'Das Selbstmodell ist ein Teil des Metamodells').
items.source: docs/decisions.md:824 (D-S366-F); master §3.2 l.209; commit 0c6044d3; drafts/aiw363-fmt-framework-check.md T1
items.bears_on: Abstract ('scope (a nesting: ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM)'): add that nesting is the normal mode, with exceptions. §2.1 scope as a continuous axis s∈[0,1] from pure self to pure world: how that axis encodes a nesting, and that the closure partner is EWM∖ESM. §4.1 'IWM = the world-knowledge partition of W; ISM = the self-knowledge partition' ('partition' vs ISM ⊆ IWM). §6.2: does O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM hold when nesting fails? §6.4: w in Ψ(e,w) should be the closure partner (EWM∖ESM, its active part). §5.3 density migration under disembodied salvinorin.
items.scope_limits: Exceptions hedged ('maybe', 'perhaps'). Nesting is representational, not neural co-location. Crucible's operational reading: world model = every explicit model outside the self model.

items.finding: Active parts and closure defined. MG, verbatim: world model = 'all explicit modeling outside the self model'; 'the part that reaches the self model would be the active world model'; 'the part of the self model that acts on the world model would be the active part of the self model'; 'the mutual updating between the active explicit self model and the active [explicit] world model would be the explicit closure that gives rise to phenomenality, the sense of being here and now' (D9: 'implicit' was a slip). Master §3.3 now reads: 'The part of the explicit world model that reaches the self model is the *active* world model, and the part of the self model that acts on the world model is the *active* self model. Their mutual updating is the closed loop, which gives the sense of being here and now, and content in it *is* experience.' T3: 'active' is reserved for this sense, and other uses become 'running' (Table 4: 'All four running').
items.source: docs/decisions.md:822 (D-S366-D (3)-(4)), :825 (T3); master §3.3 l.256, Table 4 l.709-713; ~/crucible/docs/decisions.md 2026-10-30 ~11:43 (D8, D9)
items.bears_on: §6.4: Ψ(e,w) should act on the active self and active world models, and 'closure = mutual updating' (an ongoing process) sits uneasily with a fixed point (a stationary joint state) (collector observation). §3.5 χ_loop = the fraction in the active-part loop. Terminology: the formalization uses 'active' in the old sense in §2.5 ('the EWM is the active representation'), §6.2 ('the EWM actively models') and §7.4 ('only one active at any given time').
items.scope_limits: Undeposited master edit. Terminology collision: in his 2026-10-27 spec MG also used 'active' for dynamical/prospective models ('the dynamical ones being active, prospective planning').

items.finding: Term for non-active explicit content. Keep 'preconscious' (Dehaene's sense: could enter the loop, not experienced) and add 'what psychology traditionally called the subconscious'. Implicit knowledge stays 'non-conscious'. MG (D-S366-D (5)), verbatim: 'the non active parts of world and self models would be the "subconsciousness" that the famous psycholigists are talking about'. Master §3.3: 'The non-active parts of both models are preconscious, what psychology traditionally called the subconscious (Section 3.4.6).'
items.bears_on: Terminology in §3.5 (the formalization already says 'preconscious'). It conflicts with the 2015 definition (Unterbewusstsein includes implicit knowledge, Emergenz p.69), so the formalization should not equate implicit with subconscious. Interacts with F14.
items.scope_limits: MG was first unsure ('not really sure what term is scientiffically more corect … or less poisoned by pseudoscience') and chose this after the reasoning.

items.finding: The working model (§3.6.1 channel occupancy, the 2015 Arbeitsmodell) IS the active part of the explicit models. Master §3.6.1 now reads: 'The working model is the active part of the explicit models, the active world and self models, and closure is their mutual update.' The anesthetic-dissociation sentence now reads 'If experience is the closure of the active self and world models over the channel's occupancy'. The narrow-path sentence now makes closure mutual: 'its output, fed back into the world-model's update rule while the world model updates the self model in turn, yields self-consistency'. In the same section, working-memory capacity (7±2 / 4±1) 'is the rank of the channel'.
items.bears_on: The formalization has no channel, rank or working-model object. χ_loop (§3.5) could be identified with channel occupancy (the active parts), which gives χ_loop a capacity bound (rank). §3.3 selection family G = selection into the channel. The two-dials/rank independence (master: rank is a third parameter, not a criticality dimension) is absent from §4.7.
items.scope_limits: Undeposited master edit.

items.finding: Rudimentary closure among non-active explicit models = minimal consciousness (hedged hypothesis). MG chose the 'fourth reading' of his hypothesis 'basic awareness may already arise from non active explicit models without active closure': non-active explicit models can close weakly on each other, and that rudimentary closure gives basic awareness (the paper's minimal consciousness), below the full active closure that gives 'the sense of being here and now'. Principle 3 holds (no experience without some closure). Master §3.5 now reads: 'Minimal consciousness: A rudimentary closure, consciousness at its minimum. It can arise among non-active explicit models, without the active closure that gives the full sense of being here and now.' Crucible instrument consequence: weak mutual lagged prediction among non-active directions, tested separately from active closure.
items.bears_on: §6.3 table, Minimal row ('Rudimentary closure'): add 'among non-active explicit models'. §3.5 χ_loop is binary in/out of 'the closed loop' and needs at least two grades (rudimentary vs active closure). §6.4 defines closure only for the coupled update. Collector observation: it is in tension with §3.3 'the non-active parts … are preconscious' (not experienced) and with §3.4.6 'accessible … held in an explicit model without entering the self-model's closed loop … is not conscious'.
items.scope_limits: HEDGED: MG said 'may'. It stays a hypothesis to test; MG wanted to discuss H1. The paper carries one sentence. A weak-closure test needs its own pre-stated floor (crucible: ΔR² 0.0012–0.0013 vs null 0.0003–0.0005, below the 0.01 floor).

items.finding: 'Reflective' at the floor = the self mirrored in the world model it closes with (H2). Master §3.5 minimal rung: 'The self is mirrored in the world model it closes with, without thinking about itself.' Reflection proper stays at the doubly extended rung.
items.bears_on: §6.3 recursion-depth table (μ₀ minimal/basic vs μ₁/μ₂). §6.3 self-knowledge measure R.
items.scope_limits: MG's source hypothesis 'explicit closure might already give rise to a basic reflective self' was hedged ('might').

items.finding: Open item: Principle 2's 'persistent activity patterns that survive their own inputs' (master l.137, l.240) conflicts with ruling (1) 'recurring' and, read literally, with D10's input-locked integrated model. MG (T5): the decision waits for crucible's CRU-238 input-cut result. E15 ('being here' at the floor) was not applied.
items.bears_on: Principles. §1.1 paraphrases P2 without 'survive their own inputs'; the formalization should not adopt that clause before T5 is ruled. It also bears on how explicit models are individuated in §4.1.
items.scope_limits: Pending; no ruling.

items.finding: Closure is located inside the explicit level, not in the explicit–implicit relation. Master l.297 (E11), old: 'Consciousness arises from the interplay between this cortical automaton and the substrate … from the dynamic relation between the explicit models … and the structural knowledge base'. New: 'Consciousness arises within the explicit models this automaton carries, where the explicit self and world models update each other, while the structural knowledge base generates and sustains those models.' The ICT comparison l.893 (E12) now states closure mutually: 'closure counts only where the self-model and the world model enter each other's update rules'. Fig. 3 caption (E13) now reads: 'The boundary between implicit and explicit sets what can become conscious, and the closed loop of the explicit self and world models sets what does.'
items.source: master l.297, l.387, l.893; commit 8ec0bdd8; drafts/aiw363-fmt-framework-check.md E11–E13 (rulings (4), (5))
items.bears_on: §7.2 'Consciousness is a functor F: Sub → Sim' places consciousness in the substrate-to-simulation mapping, the reading E11 removed from the master; per the ruling, consciousness lies in Sim's internal mutual update (collector observation). §2.2 'Everything above ν_crit … is conscious where it enters the self-model's closed loop' is consistent with E13: ν_crit is necessary, the loop decides.
items.scope_limits: Undeposited master edits.

items.finding: Collector observation (not a ruling): the S342 Sperling insertion may conflict with T4. Master §3.4.6 (added S342, v21): 'On FMT all the letters are seen: each is in the running simulation as an experienced item … Identification requires the system to take the item as an object and hold it in short-term memory, which has limited capacity … The seen letters are accessed in the sense defined above.' 'Accessed' content is defined as in the closed loop. T4 makes the loop = the active models = the working model = channel occupancy, whose capacity 'is the rank of the channel' (4±1). All 12 letters 'accessed' sits uneasily with a rank-4 occupancy unless rank bounds dimensionality rather than item count, which the master does not say.
items.bears_on: §3.5 χ_loop and C(t): what is in the loop versus what is reported. Any formal capacity bound on χ_loop derived from F13.
items.scope_limits: Unverified tension found by this collector; needs MG or a red-team check.

items.finding: The two criticality axes move apart (Toker et al. 2022). Waking cortex is 'slightly subcritical by its branching ratio (Priesemann et al., 2014) and slightly chaotic by its slow electrodynamics (Toker et al., 2022)'. Propofol: 'Branching: forced subcritical. Edge of chaos: deeper into the chaotic phase'. Psychedelics: 'LSD closer to the edge'. Anaesthetic convergence is now 'a displacement from the critical band: on the branching axis typically a push below it, on the edge-of-chaos axis in either direction, with propofol deeper into chaos and generalized seizures in the periodic phase'. The S357 red-team found Toker 2022 had been cited inverted elsewhere (verified PMC8851554).
items.source: master Table 4 l.711-718 + column note, §5.3 l.720, §8.1 l.959; AIW-340 (backlog.md:101; S359 commit 3e9b959a; published in v29); conversation-log.md S357 l.7564; docs/research/noc-slice-s356-audit/s357-review.md
items.bears_on: §4.2 Class mapping (σ<1 → Class 1/2, σ>1 → Class 3; λ_max<0 'ordered'): propofol is σ<1 and λ>0 at once, so the two mappings disagree. §4.3 options 1–3 and 'Empirical resolution … states where the two measures diverge': propofol and waking are now measured cases. §4.5 'deep propofol anesthesia, where cortical dynamics also turn subcritical' needs 'on the branching axis'. §3.4 Fokker-Planck propofol signature. §4.2 σ band 'slightly subcritical to slightly supercritical'.
items.scope_limits: Toker 2022 has no ketamine or sleep data. Toker et al. themselves call waking's side 'far from settled'; 'chaotic side' is inferred from their model and the LSD shift direction.

items.finding: Seizure route: now direct evidence for generalized seizures. Master §3.7 reads: 'Direct human evidence for that departure exists for both seizure types. Focal ictal recordings lose the power-law statistics of the critical regime (Meisel et al., 2012) … in the generalized seizures measured so far (two intracranial, one MEG), the slow cortical electrodynamics crossed the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022), the hypersynchrony route.' The invariant stays route-robust: 'Either route out of Class 4 … collapses the extent dimension, so the prediction of unconsciousness is robust to which ictal dynamics obtain.' §10.3 keeps 'phase- and scale-dependent rather than uniform'.
items.bears_on: §4.7 seizure as the separating case, which says 'The route out is phase- and scale-dependent and is not settled … stated route-agnostically'. That can stay route-agnostic but now omits the direct generalized-seizure evidence. didactic-patterns.md's 'Cautions' item 'Seizure (Pattern 4): route … NOT settled' (S300) predates this and is partly superseded for generalized seizures.

The decisive test is cost at matched function on an open-ended workload, never "capability dies when the loop is cut".' items.finding: Play as free modelling (MG theory point; master §6.4, v29). 'The modelling the theory requires builds in steps: a model of the organism itself, then models of other agents made by re-pointing that self-model (Section 4.2.4), then free modelling, the recruitment of open-ended computation for models that serve no present goal. In behaviour, free modelling shows as activity without an immediate payoff, and its clearest form is play.' Play's distribution (mammals, birds, octopuses, some reptiles; Burghardt 2005) 'broadly tracks the evidence for self-modelling'. Its absence does not establish absence of consciousness.
items.source: master §6.4 l.813; backlog.md:44 (AIW-347, from crucible decisions 2026-07-08/09); commit bb942797 (S360); published v29 10.5281/zenodo.23660780
items.bears_on: Definition of free modeling. The formalization §4.2/§4.5 says 'open-ended computation recruited for self-modeling'. Master Table 1b says 'recruited by the system for its own modeling'. The play paragraph says 'for models that serve no present goal' and places free modelling as a step after self-model and other-models. Three wordings to reconcile (collector observation). It also gives a behavioural observable for the free-modeling threshold.
items.scope_limits: A behavioural marker, not a criterion; tool use is a further modelling step.

items.finding: The VM tax (closure's running cost). 'The closed self-model loop is a simulation layer running on the substrate, and like any virtual machine it is slower than the hardware beneath it: on fast reactive work … the loop adds latency and loses. It pays for itself on work the substrate cannot do by mapping the present: counterfactual reasoning, long-horizon planning, extrapolating a mechanism beyond the cases seen, and optimising over a model.' Predicted signature: 'on tasks where reactive performance has plateaued and the payoff lies at a long horizon, capability scales with the internal simulation budget, the time a system is allowed to run its model before acting, when closure is in place, and stops scaling when closure is ablated (Section 8.12).'
items.source: master §4.2.4 l.623; AIW-347 (backlog.md:44); commit bb942797 (S360); v29
items.bears_on: §6.5 complexity cost of self-reference (it formalizes only capacity overhead C_total ≥ ΣC_k + overhead(n), not latency or time cost). §4.7 processing volume ∫C(t)dt. §8 Phase 4 predictions (a new formalizable prediction: performance as a function of simulation budget × closure on/off).
items.scope_limits: Fitted to the cost-window framing (didactic #18): a price, not a barrier; the scaling claim is an untested prediction.

items.finding: Body-first emergence (expectation). 'Natural emergence is also expected to start from the body. For a recurrent network coupled to a body, that body is the most persistent, most controllable and most informative regularity in its input, so the first stable attractor such a network forms is expected to model it … This is an expectation; it has not yet been measured in spiking networks.' MG's origin (AIW-302): 'the first attractor to emerge in a spiking network comes from body feedback'.

items.finding: FMT takes no stance on a stored record of a run. Master §3.4.5 (v27): 'One case lies at the edge of this distinction, and the theory takes no stance on it: a complete stored record of such a run, every state present on a medium and none computed. If experience needs physical unfolding that no pattern of states captures, the record lacks it; if structure suffices, the record has the experience the run has, and "running" names the internal dependency of a realized trajectory, not the activity of a host … the choice between them turns on physics.' MG named the two answers the 'unfolding view' and the 'structure view' (S354). Together with SUFFICIENCY-19 (S342; master l.537): 'To actually perform the computation is to realize a trajectory whose states depend on one another through an open-ended rule; the clause names that realized dependency and adds no condition on how the process unfolds in time.'
items.source: master §3.4.5 l.383, §3.7.3 l.537; docs/decisions.md:682 (SUFF-19), :735 (S354); commit 85654faf; No Outside §14.5 and §14.8 (drafts/zenodo-ready/nooutside/no-outside-draft-v1.0.md l.1046-1107)
items.bears_on: §6.4 'The function Ψ runs on the substrate; the fixed point m* is a property of the dynamics'. §7.2 functor with morphisms = 'physical dynamics'. §4.7 processing volume ('the physical clock-second entering only because the substrate runs at a finite rate') and subjective duration. §6.1 'no outside' framing. On the structure view, 'running/process' = the realized dependency structure, not execution in time.
items.scope_limits: FMT takes no side; No Outside §14.8: on the unfolding view the architecture is necessary and 'no longer sufficient'.

items.finding: The constitutive limit is perspectival (No Outside v1.0.2/v1.0.3 §14.6, §14.8). 'Description and instance are relations … One structure is a description from one side and an instance from the other'. FMT's 'reading the code is not having the experience' is 'true of the reader'. On the structure view, 'FMT's denial that a complete description is an instance survives as a statement about readers and is dropped as a statement about structures.' The bridge 'closure is phenomenality' is unchanged; what changes is what 'running' means.
items.bears_on: §6.1 ('A weather simulation … has an "outside" from which it can be fully described. A self-referential simulation has no such outside — the simulation *is* its own observer'). §6.4 ('no remainder — no "outside view"'). §6.6 ('no "more fundamental" level … it is self-contained'). §7.2 (Sim properties absent from Sub).
items.scope_limits: The revision applies only on the structure view; FMT takes no stance (F28).

items.finding: The Kleene correction and the absent-generator principle (No Outside v1.0.1+). 'The generator can appear in what it generates, even completely, but only as a finished state; the generating does not appear in its own product.' Kleene's recursion theorem and quines show that complete self-description is possible. 'Kleene's theorem is the same theorem read in the other direction' as Lawvere (1969); 'Self-reference on its own is constructive; what has no solution is self-reference with a negation in it'. The first limit 'is not' a diagonal argument. §7.1 restates FMT's observability constraint, meta-problem and unrepresentable apparatus as one limit: 'The system can hold a model of its own generation, a past state of it, even a complete description of it, and still not hold the generating it is doing now.' §7.4: 'The self-model is not a Gödel sentence, and consciousness is not explained by incompleteness'.
items.source: docs/decisions.md:703 (S346); No Outside Preface l.15-17, §5.1 l.297-320, §7.1 l.480-494, §7.4 l.529-540; commits 883bcdd1, 44c6d7f2 (AIW-316)
items.bears_on: §6.4 ties the fixed point to 'Lawvere's fixed-point theorem' and to 'no remainder'. In the Kleene direction Lawvere guarantees existence of self-reproducing fixed points and does not by itself yield a no-outside property (collector observation). §6.2 consequence 1, 'S_EWM^c inaccessible to the ESM': No Outside places the limit on the current act of generating, not on representing substrate facts as content. §6.6 RG fixed point.
items.scope_limits: Stated in No Outside (published preprint), not in the FMT master.

items.finding: Scope of formalizing consciousness, and what formalism carries. S343: 'No Outside's reading limit bounds only the strong claim (a formalism certifying that its structure *is* experience); formalising consciousness theories stays legitimate.' No Outside §15.2: 'What a formalism captures is relational structure, and that is what different observers can share, check and build on. What the symbols are, the ontology behind the structure, stays with each perspective.'
items.source: docs/decisions.md:691 (S343 'Kleiner framing'); conversation-log.md l.7480; No Outside §15.2 (l.1150-1163)
items.bears_on: §9.2 limits ('The formalization does not derive phenomenality from mathematics'). §9.1 'Sharpened transformation of the Hard Problem … a philosophical result in its own right'. §6.4 'The phenomenal properties exist at m*'. §1.3 scope.

items.finding: The readout fallacy (Auslesefehlschluss), named by MG in S351: 'Inferring the structure of a capacity from the structure of the data an instrument can read out of it' (2015 source: Emergenz p.45 Lulu, the IQ factor model only 'bedeutet, dass die Leistungsdaten, die ein typischer IQ-Test erheben kann, so strukturiert sind'). FMT Prediction 5 (v26) reads: 'A dissimilarity matrix built from similarity judgments is a readout, and taking its structure for the structure of the qualia space would commit the readout fallacy … what they recover is the relational organization of explicit content that enters a judgment … Explicit content that never enters a judgment lies outside what the test can recover.' Master §7.3 (v28) adds three carry-overs from the g case: 'The method fixes part of the structure it returns, the metric and the number of dimensions among it. A structure pooled across subjects need not hold within any one of them (Borsboom et al., 2003). And different generating structures fit the same data (van der Maas et al., 2006).' Didactic #41: 'STATE HOW FAR THE INFERENCE DOES HOLD … The fallacy is the step past that boundary, not the measurement.'
items.source: docs/decisions.md:726 (S351); master §8.6 l.1023, §7.3 l.925; RIM v8 §2.7 (paper/intelligence/paper.md:101, 10.5281/zenodo.23540278); FMT v26 10.5281/zenodo.23540275; .claude/knowledge/didactic-patterns.md #41 (l.903-924); No Outside §15.2
items.bears_on: §2.5 principal-bundle qualia structure (Oizumi, Lim & Kanai) and the formalization's own G-EED / semidirect-product prediction. §2.6 cautions (ICA/NMF/RSA decompositions return the structure of the measure; 'emergent dimensionality' says the number of axes is 'measured', yet the method fixes part of it). §5.3 RSA. §9.2 (decomposed patterns 'may be artifacts of our decomposition method'). Estimating ρ.
items.scope_limits: Name has no established prior use (S351 check). Distinct from reification, the ecological fallacy and the jingle fallacy. The psychometric half is old; the consciousness half is the new application.

items.finding: Reply to the Kleiner & Ludwig (2024b) no-go theorem (chip consciousness). Master §7.3: 'On the theory, consciousness is constituted by the self-simulation the system runs, so it adds no dynamics to the system's own computational description; the closed self-model loop is part of that description, and the difference it makes shows against other systems, in what a system without the loop fails to do at matched resources (Table 1b), not against the system's own reference dynamics. Dynamical relevance is defined relative to a reference theory … The Four-Model Theory's test presupposes relevance relative to a different reference, a matched system without the loop … consciousness is read from architecture, not as a departure from the system's own dynamics.' Kleiner & Ludwig's Synthese paper relabelled 2024a.
items.source: master §7.3 l.921; backlog.md:71 (AIW-322); commits 3fa69771 (S355), bb942797 (S360 reference-theory wording per S359 refcheck); docs/research/kleiner-ludwig-2024-reading.md

items.finding: Reply on file to Mallavarapu & Percy (2026), 'A No-Go Theorem for Process Theories of Consciousness': P1 irreducible history-dependence + P2 local-state sufficiency + P3 causal efficacy are inconsistent. Planned reply: 'every FMT constituent is a present-state fact (implicit models in weights, explicit models in current activation, closure = the self-model currently representing itself)'; reject P1. 'The temporal echo helps — the experienced "now" is constructed content, so the echo window is the latency that produces present content, not a constitutive interval.' Open: 'whether master wording ("ongoing", "running", closure as process) needs a present-state gloss'.
items.bears_on: §6.4 fixed point (a present-state condition) vs §4.7's ∫C(t)dt processing volume and the temporal echo. §7.2 functor composition over transitions. Interacts with F28 (realized-trajectory reading).

items.finding: Pattee's epistemic cut as precedent (master v21). Pattee (2001): any system that measures or controls requires an epistemic cut between rate-independent memory and rate-dependent dynamics, and the subject side needs semantic closure. 'The implicit/explicit split has this shape, with the stored implicit models on the side of memory and the running explicit models … on the side of dynamics; Pattee, however, holds the cut to be epistemic and not ontological … so his argument supports the claim that an outside description does not exhaust what such a system does and leaves the constitutive reading as this theory's own commitment.'
items.bears_on: §7.1 Sub/Sim categories and the real/virtual split; §6.1 closure and the Hard Problem; §9.2 limits (constitutive vs epistemic reading stated as a commitment).
items.scope_limits: Support for the shape only; the constitutive reading remains FMT's own commitment.

items.finding: Phenomenal concept strategy and indexical gap (master v21 §4.2.5). Reply to Chalmers' (2007) master argument: FMT grants that a conceivable zombie has the architectural fact (a closed, indexical, substrate-opaque self-model) and denies that it must entail a priori that phenomenal beliefs are true (type-B). 'On FMT the phenomenal concept is itself indexical: it is the closed self-model's access to its own states as its own. The phenomenal gap is then a gap of the indexical kind, widened by opacity … FMT needs the contrary claim, that the phenomenal gap is the indexical gap of a closed self-modeling system, and that claim is not proven here.'
items.source: master §4.2.5 l.629; commit c3ba4f9c (S342, AIW-302 'JCS-carve §6.2 indexical-gap claim'); cf. Balog 2012, Perry 1979
items.bears_on: §6.2 observability constraint consequences 1–2 ('The Meta-Problem becomes deductive', 'The Hard Problem's formulation presupposes a violation'). The master states the key identity is 'not proven', so the formalization's 'deductive' and 'architecturally impossible' should not claim more than the master.

items.finding: A second meta-problem mechanism is being tested (AIW-343). The master's §3.8 meta-problem has two mechanisms: universal opacity, and 'near-opacity punctuated by occasional leaks' (phosphenes, visual snow, hypnagogia, filling-in). S358 derived a pre-registrable prediction: trait leak frequency predicts the 'hidden depth' form of the hard-problem intuition (H1 partial r ≥ .15). Leak frequency should predict hidden-depth items more strongly than explanatory-gap items (H2). Pre-registered on OSF h4n7f (2026-10-28); Arm C live since S365.
items.bears_on: §3.4 Fokker-Planck diffusion D ('stochastic leakage … produces phenomena like visual snow and spontaneous phosphenes'): D is the formal home of the leak mechanism and could carry a trait parameter. §6.2 consequence 1 derives the meta-problem from opacity (S_EWM^c) alone; the master has two mechanisms.

items.finding: Def A, 'Pointing Is Not Defining: The Definition of Consciousness Is Not Settled', was published (theory claims touching FMT). It sets conditions on an explicatum: C1 non-circularity, C2 grounding, C3 explicit operationalization without sole reliance on first-person report, C4 substrate neutrality, C5 discrimination of contested cases, C6 'A stated bridge … stated, together with what would count against it', C7 agreement on uncontested cases, C8 explanation of the pointer (meta-problem as an adequacy test), C9 'Creature and state distinguished' (capacity vs occurrence). Footnote 6: FMT 'defines consciousness as the ongoing process in which an entity runs a model of itself … names the capacity for that process separately, and states its bridge as an identity of phenomenality with self-referential closure. For systems whose connectome, weights and running dynamics are inspectable it proposes a decision procedure that does not require report'.
items.bears_on: §2.3 note that the self-modeling requirement is 'definitional rather than empirical'. Whether ρ, θ_k and the §4.5 conjunction formalize the occurrent state or the capacity (C9). The bridge in §6.1/§6.4 and what would count against it (C6). The meta-problem consequence in §6.2 (C8).

items.finding: D21, MG in the crucible console, verbatim: 'there is a difference between world models that reside close to the sensory inputs or motoric feedback (which more or less should always reflect reality well) and abstract world models like imagining a distance place or a future event, something we probably cannot expect to find in a creature so simple without some fine tuning (as evolution would have done …)'. items.finding: Explicit models are emergent spiking ACTIVITY and never a region, population, slice or module. Only the implicit models (IWM, ISM) are substrate-level: connectome form plus weights, partly engineered as evolution did and partly trained. The explicit models come in two sorts: robust sustained patterns (what the body does and senses) and flexible, dynamical patterns (prospective planning, simulation). MG's correction: the body model takes 'a good fraction of the total cortex area', not one column. ClosureBrain (CE/EWM/ISM/ESM as region-slices) is NOT an FMT architecture. Results that rank or ablate the named regions are not FMT evidence, though they may stand as dynamics engineering. Core principle, verbatim: 'the secret is in defining, finding and analyzing spiking activita AS MODELS, thats the trick FMT offers.'

items.scope_limits: A theory and architecture ruling, unhedged. MG has NOT ruled whether it reaches the gridworld FmtAgent results (P1 causal transfer, d = 2.44), whose ESM is a module object; that is open question 2 in aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md. Structural and graph results (A#7 relocation cost, A#9 span argmin) may stand as dynamics engineering but not as evidence about model kinds.
items.bears_on: Explicit-model criterion; Phase 4 (§8): 'FMT-minus-ESM' ablation, 'ESM ablation' and the ablation-validity audit's 'efferent disconnection of one region' all treat the ESM as an ablatable part. Module 2 (l.571): transfer entropy between 'known implicit processing regions' and 'known explicit/conscious access regions'. The robust-vs-dynamical distinction does not appear anywhere in the formalization. Phase 4's 'IWM/ISM as learned substrate weights, EWM/ESM as running processes' is consistent with the ruling.

items.finding: Two substrate choices. Thalamus = BOTH: one thalamus-like relay for all I/O, AND the 'low-rank channel between explicit activity and substrate (thalamocortical loop)'. Ganglia = BOTH: peripheral sensory and motor ganglia for I/O, plus a basal-ganglia-like selector 'gating what enters the loop'. Topology: I/O through a few ganglia-like spiking networks, then ONE thalamus-like restriction, then a cortex-like sheet with Brodmann-like areas and enough free area for other things.

items.scope_limits: MG chose among aIware-written options via AskUserQuestion. These are his choices, not his words. They specify crucible's build target rather than state a theory claim.
items.bears_on: §3.3 selection family G and permeability: one low-rank thalamocortical channel between substrate and explicit activity, plus a gating selector, gives a concrete anatomical reading of the implicit-to-explicit channel and of selection. Also §4.6 (the implicit-explicit threshold).

items.finding: What it takes to say 'there are explicit models'. WRITE is confirmed: the activity follows its target better than a time-shifted null. READ, meaning actual use, is NOT required for a model; it is evidence for consciousness. D-S366-A, verbatim: 'definition of model should say it is readable, not that it is actually read. that is only required for actual consciousness'. Generated-not-stored holds by construction in a frozen network: weights are fixed, cell memory is ≤10 ms and there is no STP, so a pattern that recurs across 30-s windows must be regenerated. The vanish-and-return test was dropped. Boundary is not required: MG chose the session option 'Write is enough'. D-S366-G T7 then demoted boundary recognition from a model criterion to a consequence of the target. Crucible's operational criterion is now: recurring activity, found without labels, that passes WRITE and is readable (member cells project outside the pattern).

items.scope_limits: 'Write is enough' is MG's pick of a session-written option. Generated-not-stored holds by construction only for frozen networks with no plasticity and no STP; with learning on it needs a test again. The pre-statement deferred the readability check, a wiring check of outgoing synapses, and it is still owed for every pattern reported so far.
items.bears_on: Explicit-model criterion. §2.6 asks that modes 'correlate with behavior, stimulus content, or report' to count as real; WRITE against a time-shifted null is the stronger form of that requirement (see also C13). §6.2: 'generated from the substrate, not filled by a copy'. Any formal definition of 'model' in the formalization must use readable, not read, and must not list boundary as a criterion.

items.finding: The realistic explicit self model is a lower-dimensional, INTEGRATED MODEL of the actual self, not a 'copy'; 'copy' is retired by D-S366-H. It is integrated 'from several implicit models plus sensory input plus motor feedback etc. as needed for the entity, modulated by salience and memory'. It departs strongly from the implicit self models only in imagination ('being a horse or a chair'). Simplest form: 'a low dimensional model (not "copy") of the body or at least a viewpoint projected into the real world from which the senses seem to get their information'. D-S366-I: a viewpoint is NOT the position estimate the paper excludes. It is the origin the senses are referred to, the perspective that binds sensory input, not a coordinate on a map. Flat ruling ~11:38: 'only complexer tasks and worlds and selves can start to show a str[o]ng difference between explicit and implicit models'.
items.source: /home/jeltz/crucible/docs/decisions.md l.67-79, l.168-181, l.183-203 (the l.201 quote); /home/jeltz/aIware/docs/decisions.md l.826-827; /home/jeltz/crucible/docs/fmt-core.md.
items.scope_limits: Unhedged theory rulings. The viewpoint-vs-position distinction is a definitional ruling; no crucible test of it exists yet.
items.bears_on: Self-model criterion. The mode axis ν and the threshold ν_crit (§2.1, §4.6): in simple systems the implicit/explicit contrast is expected to be weak, which favours a graded ν and warns against expecting a sharp threshold in small substrates. §5.1: the ESM as an input-dependent attractor driven by i_self matches 'integrated from implicit models plus current input'.

items.finding: Operational closure vocabulary. World model = 'all explicit modeling outside the self model' (D19: 'all explicit models that are not the self model are world model parts'). A world-model part must itself pass WRITE; arbitrary directions of activity are not models. The ACTIVE world model is 'the part that reaches the self model'. The ACTIVE self model is 'the part of the self model that acts on the world model'. Closure = 'the mutual updating between the active explicit self model and the active explicit world model', which gives 'phenomenality, the sense of being here and now'. D9: MG's 'implicit world model' was a slip, so closure is explicit↔explicit, as in paper §3.5. Non-active parts of the explicit world and self models are 'the "subconsciousness" that the famous psychologists are talking about'. The paper term stays 'preconscious' (Dehaene's sense) plus a clause about the subconscious (D-S366-G T2). The paper adopts 'active world/self model', and the working model is the active part (T3/T4).
items.scope_limits: Unhedged rulings. D19 was a re-asked question (a session error), and MG reaffirmed the ~11:43 ruling.
items.bears_on: §6.4 defines closure as a fixed point Ψ(m*) = m* over the joint explicit state m = (e, w), with no active/non-active partition. MG's operational closure is mutual updating between the ACTIVE parts, a dynamic coupling that is not necessarily a fixed point. §3.5 χ_loop and the preconscious remainder: §3.5 already says 'preconscious', so it is consistent. §6.2: S_EWM ('the EWM actively models') may need the active/running distinction of T3.

items.finding: Nesting (ESM ⊆ EWM) is 'the normal mode of operation'. Exceptions, hedged by MG: an out-of-body experience without a body, 'like on a strong salvinorin dose with nothing for the body model to latch onto maybe', or 'the self model system being overwhelmed or damaged … maybe cotard'. 'nested doesnt necessarily mean physically at the same neural locations at the same time'; the nesting is representational, not neural co-location. The master adds: 'The part of the EWM outside the ESM … is the world model with which the self model closes.'
items.scope_limits: The nesting is a ruling. The list of exceptions is hedged ('maybe').
items.bears_on: Abstract ('scope (a nesting: ESM ⊆ EWM …)'). §6.2 observability constraint O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM, which is stated as 'architecturally constitutive' with no exceptions; the named exceptions (salvinorin OBE, damaged self model, Cotard) need a sentence. §5.1: salvinorin ESM redirection, where α → 0 of i_self is the case MG names as breaking the nesting. §6.4: the world model in the loop is EWM \ ESM.

items.finding: Hedged hypotheses, not rulings. (1) 'basic awareness may already arise from non active explicit models without active closure'. Resolved reading (D-S366-J, MG: 'fourth reading is correct'): non-active explicit models can close WEAKLY on each other, and that rudimentary closure gives basic awareness, i.e. the paper's minimal consciousness, below the full ACTIVE closure that gives 'the sense of being here and now'. Principle 3 holds: no experience without some closure. The master §3.5 now carries one sentence on this (3f03a3ef). (2) 'explicit closure might already give rise to a basic reflective self' is open. Read as reflection proper, it conflicts with §3.5 (no reflection at the floor). H2 defines 'reflective' as 'the self mirrored in the world model it closes with'. (3) S366-C: 'my suspicion: that pattern is basic consciousness already … tracks the main pain/pleasure axis … should allow the creature to follow the pain pleasure axis even if we change or remove a limb or damage a small part of the rest of the brain, IF it is stable enough, and suggests experience' and 'if rich enough it might allow the creature to model its way around a new kind of obstacle'.

items.scope_limits: Every one of these is HEDGED ('may', 'might', 'suspicion', 'probably'): a hypothesis to test, not a finding. Crucible's tests so far found no weak closure at 8k and withdrew the 40k lead (C11, C12), so crucible data do NOT support (1) or (3). Must not be written as shown.
items.bears_on: §3.5 says 'explicit content held outside that loop is preconscious'. Under D-S366-J, non-active (preconscious) explicit content can itself sit in a rudimentary closure that gives minimal consciousness, so χ_loop needs to carry degrees of closure (rudimentary vs active), not one loop. §6.3/§6.4 and the levels of consciousness: is a 'basic reflective self' consistent with a minimal rung that has no reflection?

items.finding: CRU-234 found the FIRST SIMPLE EXPLICIT SELF MODEL (MG D10, 'Explicit self-model now'). It is the free-frontal weighted area-rate direction, |corr with area rate| 0.84-0.85, in the frozen 8k creature. Fold-mean WRITE R², s0/s3/s4: hunger 0.62/0.63/0.78, pain 0.08/0.10/0.24, hand-danger distance 0.22/0.21/0.28. Circular-shift null99 ≈ 0, recurring in both halves of the record. It is integrated (≥2 body variables in 3/3), BUT it adds nothing beyond the insula's relayed signal: insula rate→hunger R² 0.83/0.87 against frontal 0.62/0.77, and frontal beyond insula −0.0007/+0.0009 against a 0.01 floor. Pain beyond insula appears in 1/3 seeds only (s4, ΔR² 0.013). The combining happens in the insula; the frontal direction carries it on. At 40k (s0/s3): hunger 0.38/0.67 and pain 0.09/0.23, neither beyond the insula; hand-danger distance FAILS (−0.02/−0.13). Hand position is absent from the free areas (R² ≈ −0.04).
items.scope_limits: In silico. Frozen (learning off) LIF creature, 8k cells (3 seeds) and 40k (2 of 3 seeds analysed), on one fixed forage task, with 24-min recordings. RAW: §3-§4 had one Fable red-team, §6 (integration) none. The pre-statement EXCLUDED area-rate modes from being claimed. The 'model' status is MG's post-hoc ruling (D7 hedged 'i'd say probably yes', resolved by D10), so it is not a pre-stated positive. Readability (outgoing synapses) is still owed. It is an input-locked relay of the interoceptive signal (robust kind). Danger proximity did not replicate at 40k, and hand-danger distance passes in almost every area, probably via pain (unchecked). The fmt-core file and the handover summarise it as 'hunger + pain'. May NOT claim: closure, consciousness, a model beyond an input echo, emergence of an abstract self model, or behaviour use.
items.bears_on: Self-model criterion: it instantiates C04's 'low-dimensional integrated model of the body' in its simplest, input-locked form. §5.1: e(t+1) = h(e(t), i_self): the found ESM is i_self-driven. Phase 4 and any 'computational validation' sentence: this is the first explicit-model result on the post-10-27 substrate.

items.finding: The pleasure side of the self model is missing. The body has no pleasure sense: the senses are joints, effort + hunger, the retina and pain, and meal reward reaches only the dopamine signal, which is inert with learning off. A meal acts on the brain only by removing hunger: one item removes 0.5, the creature eats every 4-6 s, and hunger sits at 0-0.12. Event-locked, in SD units, the self direction falls after meals (−0.26/−0.31/−0.49 at 8k; −0.30/−0.35 at 40k) and jumps within 100 ms of pain onset (+0.66/+0.75/+0.70). The axis runs from 'bad' to 'neutral' and has no positive pole. MG D11 adds a taste sense (CRU-240, not built).
items.scope_limits: Descriptive, with an event-locked circular-shift null band of ±0.06-0.10. In silico, 3 seeds at 8k and 2 at 40k, frozen. The missing pole is a property of this body design, not a theory result.
items.bears_on: Self-model content and valence. Any formalization statement that the minimal ESM tracks a pain/pleasure axis: in crucible only the pain/relief half exists so far.

items.finding: World-model parts. In the free frontal/temporal areas: none at 8k (0/3; 34-37 directions per seed, each tested on 12 targets beyond the hunger route). SENSORY-NEAR world-model parts exist in the visual area: food x/y, danger x/y and hand-danger distance in 3/3 at 8k, and food/danger/neutral object in 2/2 at 40k. The body areas (S1, parietal, M1, insula) carry self-model parts. MG D21 ruling (unhedged): world models near sensory input or motor feedback, which track reality, are distinct from abstract world models such as a distant place or a future event. Hedged: abstract ones are 'probably' not to be found in so simple a creature without evolution-like fine-tuning (CRU-241), and sit in parietal/temporal/frontal ('i would guess').
items.scope_limits: RAW and NOT red-teamed (the §13-15 red-team is owed). The visual world-model parts are the retina relay, input-locked and robust. Hand-danger distance passing in nearly every area is likely a pain route (re-test with pain lags covaried is owed). S1 world passes at 40k s0 may come via touch or pain (unchecked). Frozen creature, fixed task. May NOT claim an abstract or dynamical world model.
items.bears_on: The scope axis s and the sensory-near vs abstract distinction: this is a new distinction inside the EWM that the formalization lacks. §2.7 modality-flatness: at this scale the free areas carry no world content, which matches §2.7's warning that small substrates have nothing to discriminate. Phase 4 prediction 3 (EWM coverage limits ESM) now has measurable EWM parts to manipulate.

items.finding: NO CLOSURE found. (a) Rudimentary or weak closure (Amendment D): the self direction against each other stable direction, both ways, beyond each target's own past and the insula, with a family-wise null. 8k: 0/3 seeds, only tiny one-way edges at about 0.001 of variance in s0 and s4. (b) Closure between the frontal self model and the visual world-model parts (Amendment E2). Base: own past + all seven area rates + pain + other frontal and visual directions; null: 100 random rotations within the same pattern spans. 8k 0/3 (best pairs s0 0.0021/−0.00001, s3 0.00064/0.00031 against null99 0.00032, 'at the edge', s4 ≈ 0); 40k 0/2 (s0 0.0031/−0.0002 against 0.0027; s3 0.0067/−0.0001 against 0.0057). Only the self→world direction shows anything, and only at the arbitrary-direction level. Also no active world model and no active self model at 8k (Amendment C: the other ~35 directions do not predict the candidate 100-500 ms ahead, and vice versa 0 of 34-37).
items.scope_limits: RAW. §9 and §14-15 are not red-teamed. In silico, frozen creature, linear lagged prediction over 100-500 ms, limited power (about 175 predictors cost ~0.01 CV R² by themselves). It is a null in a frozen cortex whose self model is a relayed body signal and whose world parts are the retina relay. It is not a test of closure in a learning or tuned substrate. Must not be quoted as evidence against FMT closure.
items.bears_on: Closure operationalization (§6.4): crucible's operational test is mutual lagged prediction between active explicit parts beyond common input, against a rotation null. Neither D-S366-J's rudimentary-closure hypothesis nor S366-C's 'basic consciousness already' is supported by any crucible result.

items.finding: RETRACTED: the 40k 'weak closure 2/2' lead (§10; s0 mutual j = 0, 4 at 0.029/0.033; s3 j = 2, 3) was withdrawn after a Fable red-team, independently confirmed in session. (1) Basis dependence: random rotations of the frontal ICA basis inside the same shared subspace give 'weak closure' in 3 of 4 rotations, each time with different partners. As operationalised, a FROZEN RANDOM RECURRENT NET passes the test, because any two projections of one recurrent network predict each other 100-500 ms ahead, and the circular-shift null destroys every coupling, so it cannot see this. (2) Common input from M1: corr(self, M1 rate) is 0.754 in s0. With insula + M1 lags in the base, s0 shows no pass in either direction. (3) 'Food position beyond hand' is the hunger route; with hunger covaried, food x drops 0.066 → −0.017. Methodological consequence stated by crucible: base = own past + input + ALL area rates + all other shared directions; null = random rotations of the basis (the pair must beat arbitrary directions of the same subspace); circular shift kept only as a floor.
items.scope_limits: The correction is verified: red-team plus an independent session check. The 8k Amendment D test (C11a) used the same circular-shift design, so it is permissive by construction. Its null is still a null, but that test design is not a valid closure measure.
items.bears_on: Closure operationalization (§6.4) and §3.1 transfer entropy. Any lagged-prediction or transfer-entropy measure of closure or permeability between two projections of one recurrent substrate is generically non-zero. The formalization's TE permeability and any closure statistic need a rotation (arbitrary-direction) null and conditioning on common input, not only a time-shift surrogate.

items.finding: Estimating activity-models from spikes has failure modes the formalization's §2.6 only gestures at. (a) Resolution: in 30-s windows of ~4000 cells, a perfectly stationary rank-1 pattern is matched across two windows at |cos| 0.7 only at sample eigenvalue ≈ 6.8 (spiked-covariance bound; planted 0/7 at 5-6.2, 7/7 at 8.7-10.7). ICA lost a stationary smooth mode in 4/7 pairs. (b) Over whole records, free areas hold ~18-20 stable shared directions (eigenvalues 1.4-1.6 against an MP bound of ~1.23), shared between halves at cos² > 0.5. Fixed wiring guarantees that sharing (shifted control → 0), so stability alone carries no content. (c) Basis dependence: random rotations in the same shared subspace give 8-9 of 18 'counting' directions in s4 against 2 for ICA, so the claim rule would have fired under a random basis. A pattern claim needs a rotation-invariant subspace test or a basis criterion stated in advance. (d) 'Beyond the area rate' was the wrong guard; the input area's rate must be the covariate. (e) Drifting targets (danger position, corr with time −0.48) create false negatives unless scored against a fold-mean baseline.
items.scope_limits: Methodological findings on crucible's LIF sheets and estimators (ICA, Marchenko-Pastur thresholding, ridge WRITE). The bounds are specific to window length, cell count and threshold.
items.bears_on: §2.6 'Discretization artifacts': requiring that ICA/NMF modes 'correlate with behavior' is not enough, because any rotation of a content-carrying subspace also correlates. Individuation must be rotation-invariant or pre-stated. Module 1 (§8, 'estimate ρ … ICA, NMF … Build a minimal computational model (recurrent spiking network) and estimate ρ'): estimation needs long records, input-area covariates and drift-robust scoring.

items.finding: CRU-227 P1, 'does the first lasting activity pattern model the body?', came out NOT TESTABLE under the pre-registered judge. 40k cortex, 10 simulated min per arm. No lasting object appeared in any of the 8 plasticity-on runs (BODY, REPLAY, DOT-ONLY, MIN-RANK). FROZEN's 3-4 'objects' are ONE effort-driven insula input-echo rate mode. The inhibitory homeostasis rule (ρ0 = 3 Hz on all cortical E cells, about 1,000× faster than biology) erased that mode within minutes: insula 10.0 → 2.7 Hz, and the effort→insula pathway lost 61% under the depression-biased STDP. The body barely reached the cortex (S1 joint variance 0.20 → 0.07; other areas ≈ 0), and there was no efference copy. The learning-arm null sits below the tracker's floor (C13a).
items.source: /home/jeltz/crucible/docs/results/cru227-p1-2026-10-28.md §1-§6; /home/jeltz/crucible/docs/results/cru227-m1-gate-2026-10-28.md (43,700 neurons stable 10 model-min, weights still drifting).
items.scope_limits: The may-say text is fixed in §3/§6. MUST NOT say: 'no self-model/body model formed', 'evidence against P1/FMT', 'consistent with P1', 'plasticity prevents body models', or 'FROZEN formed 3-4 stable objects'. The creature (v1) is retired for this question.
items.bears_on: Phase 4 (§8) offers 'Local homeostatic plasticity … drives deep networks … toward a common critical state (Vock & Meisel, 2026)' as an alternative to tuning. Crucible now has a record of a fast inhibitory homeostat erasing the only input-driven mode (also flagged in S365 open question 1). Also bears on transfer and consolidation dynamics under plasticity (C15).

items.finding: Rulings on learning and emergence. (1) 'strengthening and weakening must be balanced, evolution made brains that are more or less stable in their overall mapping.' (2) Random flailing should weaken the body model (slightly), but targeted behaviour from innate priors 'shold result in optimizing movement and refining priors to the point that new more efficient automatisms are learned.' (3) Innate priors are hardwired below the cortex, the cortex starts naive and unlabelled, and plasticity is reward-gated (MG's choice of session options). (4) The efference copy goes via the thalamus. (5) 10-29: sensory and motor mapping should arise 'because of the wiring structure alone, no additional mechanism needed. That is evolutions job. The interesting stuff should happen in parts of the cortex that are less directly connected to the thalamus.' (6) 10-29: the critic is parked; 'not a mechanism trying to train the cortex to build models, that would never work' (ruling). A slow 'hormone' signal after long suffering or pleasure is hedged ('I guess'). A hippocampus should be added.
items.scope_limits: Items (1), (2), (5) and (6, first half) are unhedged rulings. (3) and (4) are MG's choices of session-written options. The hormone-signal remark is hedged. These are design and theory directions with no crucible result behind them yet; the CRU-231/233 learning runs were diagnostics (C16).
items.bears_on: Transfer and consolidation, the explicit→implicit automatization MG describes in (2), which the formalization does not model (it treats only implicit→explicit permeability). Emergence vs construction framing in Phase 4 (models must emerge from wiring, never be trained in). §2.7 engine localization: MG expects free modelling away from the thalamic relay.

items.finding: CRU-231/232/233 learning runs on the v2 forage creature (8k). The first learning twins ran UNNORMALISED (normalise_incoming was never called), so they are a runaway-plasticity diagnostic, not a learning result. With normalisation (seed 0), the S1 readout stayed in the frozen band at minutes 1-2; low minutes later coincided with high pain (n = 1). The critic line was parked, and nothing showed that critic-driven learning changed behaviour. Reflex-only control (all 4000 cortex→motor-ganglion weights zeroed): 149 meals against 139 for the cortex-intact frozen twin in 10 min. The reflexes do all the eating. MG: 'That the creature can survive without cortex is expected.'
items.scope_limits: n = 1-3, RAW, with must-not-say lists in each file. Must NOT say that learning changed eating or avoidance, that the critic predicts, or that the efference copy harms learning.
items.bears_on: The read/use criterion: nothing shows the creature's behaviour reads its cortical models. Under C03, models need not be read, but without actual reading no consciousness claim is licensed. Phase 4 framing: no behavioural signature of explicit models in this creature yet.

items.finding: CRU-226 ran van der Vlag's TVB-Reservoir (commit 8606b72) unmodified via a CuPy NVRTC shim (fidelity 8.9e-8). His DFA routine, as his pipeline calls it, does NOT measure the DFA exponent. It returns ≈0.59 whether the true α is 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 or 0.9, and changes with signal units (−0.56/0.59/1.74 for ×0.01/×1/×100). Four defects cause this: region-major vs time-major indexing, no profile (cumulative sum), a sum instead of a mean of window RMS, and the median of log F / log n instead of a regression. A four-part fix matches crucible's dfa_alpha to four decimals. His Rosenstein Lyapunov core is correct, with three qualifications: a units factor of exactly ×10; strong sensitivity to the 250-sample window and fit length; and 'a provably stable linear system driven by noise reads POSITIVE'. So in a driven reservoir a positive λ is not by itself evidence of chaos. His chapter reports no nulls or surrogates, and its 'PCI' is not Casali's PCI (no source modelling or significance binarisation; values up to 3.0).
items.scope_limits: These findings concern a third party's code and pipeline, not cortex data or FMT. MG D3: offer it as a gift only once the instrument exchange is agreed, never raised cold or published as a correction. The chapter's figures are read by an aIware subagent; the readings were verified S366.
items.bears_on: §4.2 'λ_max > 0: chaotic': for driven systems, time-series λ estimates need a noise-driven linear null or a tangent-space (exact Jacobian) estimate. DFA α guidance: profile plus log-log regression over a stated range, and enough samples (625 is short). §4.7: the PCI/LZc→K mapping must specify real PCI, not 'normalised spatiotemporal LZ'.

items.finding: The CRU-226 'Must NOT claim' list consolidates crucible's status as of 10-27. Criticality is not a requirement, and there is ONE edge-related peak, in the ordered regime. Never say 'σ≈1' or 'our systems operate at criticality': branching-ratio readings are rate statements (CRU-194/198, a subsampled σ reaches unity on firing rate alone and must sit beside a rate-matched surrogate). No closure-necessity claim (five kills plus the stationary-closure theorem; route A closed ≈ capacity-matched open). A#1 'closure maintains a model' is WITHDRAWN. A#6 survives only as slow-reservoir memory. The unbounded-membrane artifact falsified the CRU-87 ladder, CRU-153 K1/K3, CRU-204b and the CRU-204 depth rungs; the CRU-36 re-entry null is AT RISK and not re-run. Nothing above 30k neurons has had a task or criticality measurement, and the scaled matched-function test is undesigned. The CRU-108 energy result is WITHDRAWN; its 39.5× connection result stands. Loop arms are materialised dense products (storage and wiring claims only). Self/world differentiation is hardcoded. CRU-222 (MG 2026-10-22): no FlowBody simulation result is quotable until the seeding defect is fixed. The fix landed 2026-10-27 for future runs; old results were not re-run.
items.scope_limits: A status list, not new data. Pre-baseline findings are included because crucible restated them after 2026-10-19.
items.bears_on: §4.2: σ carries no rate-matched surrogate requirement in the formalization. Phase 4: 'Computational validation is reported in the companion (Gruber, 2026d)', and the companion carries stale items (§6 CRU-36 'clean null', §4.5 A#6 as closure, §5 region-labelled ClosureBrain, a §8 sentence predating CRU-108).
