Let m = (e, w) be the joint explicit state, with e the ESM state and w the EWM state, and define a map Ψ: M → M, Ψ(e, w) = ($h_{e}$(e, w), $h_{w}$(e, w)), in which each model's update takes the other as input. Self-referential closure occurs when: Ψ(m\*) = m\*
findings.problem: Three mismatches with the master at HEAD. (a) The master now defines closure as the mutual updating of the ACTIVE self model (the part of the ESM that acts on the world model) and the ACTIVE world model (the part of the EWM that reaches the self model); the non-active parts are preconscious. Ψ acts on the whole joint explicit state (e, w) with no active/non-active partition, so §3.5's χ_loop (fraction of activity in the closed loop) has no definition anywhere in the paper. (b) With ESM ⊆ EWM (the paper's own abstract), w contains e, so 'each model's update takes the other as input' is degenerate unless w is the closure partner EWM∖ESM, which the master names explicitly. (c) A fixed point is a stationary joint state; the master's closure is an ongoing process ('the pass back over what the channel holds', 'Their mutual updating is the closed loop'), and the stationary-closure theorem recorded in prediction-framing.md makes a stationary loop exactly the case where closure provably buys nothing. The fixed point can stay as a special case, not as the definition.
findings.evidence: Master §3.3 l.256 ('The part of the explicit world model that reaches the self model is the *active* world model, and the part of the self model that acts on the world model is the *active* self model. Their mutual updating is the closed loop'); §3.2 l.209 ('The part of the EWM outside the ESM … is the world model with which the self model closes'); §3.6.1 l.444; decisions.md D-S366-D (3)-(4), D-S366-G T3/T4; findings F10, F11, F13, C05, C11, C12; .claude/knowledge/prediction-framing.md l.70-72 (stationary-closure theorem).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the opening of §6.4 with: 'Let the joint explicit state be m = (e, w), with e the ESM state and w the state of the world model outside the self model, EWM∖ESM (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.2). Write e_a ⊆ e for the active self model, the part of e that enters the update of w, and w_a ⊆ w for the active world model, the part of w that enters the update of e (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.3). Closure holds over a window when the coupled update Ψ(e, w) = (h_e(e, w_a), h_w(w, e_a)) is mutual: e_a and w_a each carry information about the other\'s next state beyond their own past and beyond their common input. χ_loop(s, ν, t) in Section 3.5 is the fraction of the activity at (s, ν) that lies in e_a ∪ w_a. A fixed point Ψ(m*) = m* is the stationary special case; the theory does not require it, and a loop held at a fixed point does no work a feedforward copy could not do, so the condition is mutual dependence in the update, not stationarity.' Keep the Lawvere/Kauffman paragraph only as commentary on the stationary case (see theory-6).

findings.section: 4.2 Three Candidate Criticality Measures; 4.3 Disambiguating Criticality Types; 4.5 The Two Thresholds as a Conjunction
findings.quote:
- σ < 1: subcritical (activity dies out) → Wolfram Class 1/2
- σ = 1: critical → Wolfram Class 4
- σ > 1: supercritical (activity explodes) → Wolfram Class 3
findings.problem: Since AIW-340 (S359, published in v29) the master states that the two criticality axes move apart with measured cases: waking cortex is slightly subcritical by branching ratio and slightly chaotic by its slow electrodynamics; propofol is forced subcritical on the branching axis and deeper into the chaotic phase on the edge-of-chaos axis (Toker et al., 2022). Under the paper's two mappings the same propofol state is Class 1/2 (σ < 1) and Class 3 (λ_max > 0) at once, so the σ→Class mapping is false as a class assignment. §4.3's 'Empirical resolution: compare PCI … against σ and λ_max independently, particularly in states where the two measures diverge' describes as future work what the master now reports as measured for waking and propofol. §4.5's 'deep propofol anesthesia, where cortical dynamics also turn subcritical' is true only on the branching axis. The λ_max labels also clash with the Fig. 1a ruling (axis ends 'periodic / stable' and 'chaotic / unstable', states drawn as regions). Toker 2022 is cited nowhere in the formalization.
findings.evidence: Master Table 4 l.711-718 and column note ('The two axes move apart: waking cortex is slightly subcritical by its branching ratio (Priesemann et al., 2014) and slightly chaotic by its slow electrodynamics (Toker et al., 2022)'); §5.3 l.720; §8.1 l.959; decisions.md D-S360-3 (l.772); findings F19, F21; backlog AIW-340.
findings.proposed_fix: §4.2: drop the Wolfram-class arrows from the σ list (keep 'subcritical / critical / supercritical') and add after the λ_max list: 'The two axes are measured on different signals and need not agree. In human cortex they do not: waking is slightly subcritical by branching ratio (Priesemann et al., 2014) and slightly on the chaotic side by its slow electrodynamics (Toker et al., 2022), and propofol pushes the branching axis below critical while moving the electrodynamics deeper into the chaotic phase; LSD moves them closer to the edge (Toker et al., 2022). Class 4 is therefore not read off either scalar alone, and states are regions on each axis, not points.' Relabel λ_max < 0 as 'periodic / stable' and λ_max > 0 as 'chaotic / unstable'. §4.3: replace the 'Empirical resolution' sentence with 'The two measures already diverge in waking and under propofol (Toker et al., 2022); the open question is which of them, if either, tracks consciousness across the remaining states.' §4.5: 'where cortical dynamics also turn subcritical on the branching axis'. Add Toker et al. (2022) to the references (entry as in the master, l.1916).

findings.section: 8. Phased Build Order — Phase 2 Module 4 and Phase 4: Computational Validation
findings.quote: Computational validation is reported in the companion (Gruber, 2026d); the specification below does not depend on those results.
findings.problem: Four points. (a) 'Computational validation is reported' overstates the companion as it stands: A#1 ('closure maintains a model') is withdrawn, no FlowBody result is quotable (CRU-222), the CRU-36 re-entry null is at risk and not re-run, A#6 is slow-reservoir memory, and the §5 region-labelled ClosureBrain is withdrawn as FMT evidence by the 2026-10-27 activity-not-regions ruling (AIW-361, companion v7 not yet written). (b) Module 4 ('a minimal computational model with a self-model unit'), the 'FMT-minus-ESM' arm, Prediction 1's 'ESM ablation' and the audit's 'efferent disconnection of one region' all treat the ESM as a unit that can be removed. MG's ruling: explicit models are activity emerging from the implicit substrate, 'NOT REGIONS IN A NETWORK'; results that rank or ablate named regions are not FMT evidence. A module-ESM agent is a construction and must be labelled as such. (c) The reservoir bullet ('the spectral radius tunes the substrate's open-ended computational *capability*, and the edge is not where that capability peaks') overstates CRU-203: only shallow, memory-bound tasks were measured, none open-ended. (d) The ablation-validity audit omits the finding that in the existing closure-on/off constructs no matched operating point exists (CRU-40, CRU-58: closure_enabled=False yields two closed uncoupled systems).
findings.evidence: Findings F23, F24, C01, C18, C19, C20; decisions.md D-S365-B (l.818); docs/sources/mg-2026-10-27-fmt-substrate-spec.md; .claude/knowledge/prediction-framing.md l.70; docs/research/aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md (Q19, open questions 2-3); master §3.2 l.209 ('functionally distinguished, two stored as structure and two generated as processes, not anatomically localized regions'); registry fmt-misconception-registry.md #5.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Replace with: 'In-silico tests of component mechanisms are reported in the companion (Gruber, 2026d) at toy, reservoir and gridworld scale, with the limits stated there and in its current version; the specification below does not depend on them.' (b) Module 4: 'Build a minimal computational model in which a self-model is either emergent activity on a recurrent substrate or, where it is built in, labelled as a construction, and demonstrate input-dependent identity switching under perturbation.' Phase 4 list: replace 'FMT-minus-ESM' with 'loop-cut (closure ablated against a matched baseline)', and add after the four-model bullet: 'In an emergent substrate the explicit models are activity, so an ablation targets the write/read path or the loop between self and world activity, never a labelled unit; an agent whose ESM is a module by construction tests the architecture as a construction, not its emergence.' Audit paragraph: replace 'efferent disconnection of one region' with 'disconnection of one labelled component', and add: 'The audit must also show that the two arms sit at a matched operating point; where disabling closure produces two closed systems rather than none, or shifts the operating point, the contrast is not closure against its absence.' (c) Reservoir bullet: 'the spectral radius tunes the substrate's regime, and on the shallow memory-bound tasks measured so far performance peaked in the ordered regime rather than at the edge (Section 4.4); no open-ended capability has been measured in a rate reservoir.'

findings.section: 2.1 The Model Space; 4.1 The Substrate as a Dynamical System (vs Abstract)
findings.quote: - **Scope** s(m) ∈ [0, 1]: a continuous axis from pure self-representation (0) to pure world-representation (1).
findings.problem: The abstract states scope as a nesting (ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM), but §2.1 defines the scope axis as a contrast between two disjoint poles ('pure self' vs 'pure world'), and §4.1 defines 'IWM = the world-knowledge partition of W. ISM = the self-knowledge partition of W', a partition being disjoint by definition. The master now adds that nesting is the normal mode of operation with hedged exceptions (self model with nothing to latch onto, overwhelmed or damaged; perhaps disembodied salvinorin ego dissolution, Cotard), that nesting is representational and not neural co-location, and that the closure partner is EWM∖ESM. None of this is in the paper, and the current axis definition cannot express a nesting.
findings.evidence: Master §3.2 l.209 ('Nesting is the normal mode of operation: a system models itself within its world model … It can fail when the self model has nothing to latch onto or is overwhelmed or damaged, perhaps in disembodied ego dissolution under salvinorin A or in Cotard\'s delusion'); decisions.md D-S366-F (l.824); findings F10, C06; paper abstract l.15.
findings.proposed_fix: §2.1: 'Scope s(m) ∈ [0, 1]: the extent of the model\'s target, from the self alone (0) to everything the system models, the self included (1). Scope is a nesting, not a contrast: a self model\'s target is a proper part of the world model\'s, which is the ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM of the parent theory. Nesting is the normal mode of operation and is representational, not a claim that the two share neural locations; the parent theory names hedged exceptions in which the self model has nothing to latch onto or is overwhelmed or damaged (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.2). The world model with which the self model closes is the explicit mass outside the self-scope region (Section 6.4).' §4.1: 'IWM = the world-knowledge stored in W; ISM = the part of it that is knowledge of the system itself (ISM ⊆ IWM).' Abstract: 'scope (a nesting: ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM, the normal mode of operation)'.

findings.quote: 1. **The Meta-Problem becomes deductive.** The system's inability to explain its own phenomenality is not a contingent limitation but a structural consequence of $O_{\mathrm{ESM}}$ ⊆ $S_{\mathrm{EWM}}$.
findings.problem: Three misalignments. (a) The master's own treatment is weaker: §4.2.5 grants that a conceivable zombie has the architectural fact and says the identity FMT needs 'is not proven here'; §3.8 gives two meta-problem mechanisms (universal opacity, and near-opacity punctuated by leaks), while consequence 1 derives the meta-problem from opacity alone and consequence 2 calls complete self-access 'architecturally impossible'. No Outside locates the limit on the current act of generating, not on representing substrate facts as content (the generator 'can appear in what it generates, even completely, but only as a finished state'), so 'S_EWM^c inaccessible to the ESM' states the wrong limit: substrate facts can enter the content via permeability (the paper's own consequence 3 says so). (b) Consequence 2 answers the Hard Problem as if it were asked from inside the system; the master's transformation concerns an outside description not exhausting the perspective, and says the brain does not model the scanning neuroscientist. (c) O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM is called 'architecturally constitutive' with no exceptions; when nesting fails (theory-4) the set-theoretic form can fail while the level form (the ESM represents only properties above ν_crit) survives.
findings.evidence: Master §4.2.5 l.629 ('FMT needs the contrary claim … and that claim is not proven here'); §3.8 l.543-553 (two mechanisms); §3.4.3 l.323 ('A neuroscientist scanning the brain is not thereby modeled by the brain'); No Outside Preface l.15-17, §7.1 l.480-494 (F30); findings F29, F30, F36, F37, C06.
findings.proposed_fix: Consequence 1: 'The Meta-Problem follows from the architecture. The mechanisms generating the simulation are outside S_EWM except where permeability draws them in, so the ESM meets a principled opacity when it models the basis of its own experience; the parent theory adds a second mechanism, near-opacity punctuated by leaks (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.8), which the diffusion term D of Section 3.4 can carry. The limit is on the current act of generating, which cannot appear in its own product; past states and even a complete description of the generator can (Gruber, 2026f).' Consequence 2: 'The Hard Problem presupposes that an outside description exhausts what the system does. The constraint gives that presupposition an architectural form: the perspective constituted by the closed loop is not among the properties an outside description of S_EWM lists. Whether this makes the question ill-posed depends on the constitutive reading of closure, which the parent theory argues for rather than proves (Gruber, 2026, Sections 3.4.3, 4.2.5).' Add after the model-space form: 'The invariant form is the level form: the ESM represents only properties above ν_crit. The set form O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM holds in the normal nested mode (Section 2.1).'

findings.section: 6.4 (Lawvere paragraph), 6.6 Self-Referential Closure as a Renormalization Group Fixed Point, Phase 3 Module 5
findings.quote: There is no "more fundamental" level from which the fixed point could be analyzed — it is self-contained.
findings.problem: (a) §6.4 ties 'no remainder — no outside view' to a fixed point 'related to Lawvere's fixed-point theorem', and Module 5 asks whether the fixed-point condition entails the no-outside property. No Outside (published, v1.0.3) reads Lawvere in the Kleene direction: self-reference on its own is constructive and guarantees complete self-description; the limit is that the generating does not appear in its own product, 'is not' a diagonal argument, and 'consciousness is not explained by incompleteness'. A fixed point therefore cannot be what yields no-outside. (b) §6.6's 'self-contained … no more fundamental level' contradicts the master ('This does not remove the third-person standpoint — this theory occupies one') and No Outside's perspectival reading (one structure is a description from one side and an instance from the other). (c) The paper takes a stance the master refuses: 'The function Ψ runs on the substrate; the fixed point m* is a property of the dynamics' and §4.7's clock-bound processing volume read as the unfolding view, while the master says the theory takes no stance between unfolding and structure views and SUFFICIENCY-19 defines 'actually perform' as realized dependency with no condition on unfolding in time. (d) §6.6's Wetterich dual is proved for reversible automata; cortical dynamics are dissipative, and the cosmology paper limits the correspondence to the implicit/explicit axis (S333), so 'the same mathematical object' overreaches.
findings.proposed_fix: §6.4, replace the two 'no remainder' sentences with: 'A fixed point of a self-referential map is a well-defined object (Lawvere, 1969; Kauffman, 1987), and in the constructive direction of the same theorem (Kleene) it shows that a complete self-description is possible. The parent theory\'s inside/outside asymmetry is not that result: it concerns the act of generating, which does not appear in its own product, while past states and a complete description of the generator can (Gruber, 2026f). Formalizing the asymmetry is therefore a limit on the current update step, not a property of m*. The theory takes no stance on whether a complete stored record of the trajectory has the experience the run has (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.4.5); "runs on the substrate" here names the realized dependency of the trajectory and adds no condition on unfolding in time.' §6.6 last two paragraphs: replace 'There is no "more fundamental" level … self-contained' with 'at an RG fixed point the description is the same at every scale; an outside description still exists and captures the structure, as it does in the parent theory', and qualify the identity: 'Wetterich\'s equivalence is proved for reversible automata, and cortical dynamics are dissipative, so whether a dual exists for the cortical automaton is unchecked; the companion cosmology (Gruber, 2026c) limits the correspondence to the implicit/explicit axis, and the two fixed points are offered as the same kind of object, not the same object.' Module 5: replace the no-outside goal with 'whether the asymmetry of the current generating step can be given a formal statement distinct from the fixed point'.

findings.quote: Consciousness is a **functor** F: Sub → Sim that maps substrate dynamics to simulation dynamics while preserving compositional structure:
findings.problem: The master's E11 edit moved consciousness out of the substrate-to-simulation relation and into the explicit level: 'Consciousness arises within the explicit models this automaton carries, where the explicit self and world models update each other, while the structural knowledge base generates and sustains those models.' A functor Sub → Sim formalizes generation, which the master calls self-simulation (Table 1), not consciousness, which is closure inside Sim. Two further constraints now in the master: Sim morphisms must not be 'experiential transitions' for all of Sim, only for the active loop (theory-8), and the Kleiner & Ludwig reply requires that consciousness add no dynamics to the system's computational description, so Sim's morphisms must be the image of Sub's, with no independent dynamics.
findings.evidence: Master l.297 (E11, commit 8ec0bdd8); Table 1 'Self-simulation' l.166; §7.3 l.921 ('it adds no dynamics to the system\'s own computational description'); findings F17, F33.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'Self-simulation is a functor F: Sub → Sim that maps substrate dynamics to explicit-model dynamics while preserving compositional structure. Consciousness is a structure inside Sim: the closure of Section 6.4 between the active self model and the active world model, an endo-relation on the objects F produces. Sim\'s morphisms are the images of Sub\'s transitions and add no dynamics of their own, which is what lets the theory decline the premise of the chip no-go theorem (Gruber, 2026, Section 7.3; Kleiner & Ludwig, 2024b); phenomenal change is the restriction of those morphisms to the closed loop.' Rename the subsection 'The Self-Simulation Functor'.

findings.section: 3.5 Total Conscious Content; 6.3 Self-Referential Depth via Recursive Representation (levels table)
findings.quote: Explicit content is phenomenal only where it enters the closed loop of self-model and world-model (§6.4); explicit content held outside that loop is preconscious (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.4.6).
findings.problem: χ_loop is binary in/out of 'the closed loop', and the §6.3 Minimal row reads 'Rudimentary closure; same depth as basic, poorer content'. The master now carries MG's hedged hypothesis (D-S366-J, 'may'): minimal consciousness 'can arise among non-active explicit models, without the active closure that gives the full sense of being here and now', i.e. a weak closure among content that is otherwise preconscious. Under the paper's definition such content has χ_loop = 0 and C(t) = 0, so the formalization assigns minimal consciousness no conscious content. It also lacks the 'subconscious' clause (T2) and the floor's 'self mirrored in the world model it closes with' (H2). Scope: the master states this in one hedged sentence; the paper may carry it only as a hypothesis with its own test floor.
findings.evidence: Master §3.5 l.401 ('It can arise among non-active explicit models, without the active closure …'; 'The self is mirrored in the world model it closes with, without thinking about itself'); §3.3 l.256 ('The non-active parts of both models are preconscious, what psychology traditionally called the subconscious'); decisions.md D-S366-J, D-S366-G T2, D-S366-H H2; findings F12, F14, F15; crucible C07, C11 (no weak closure found; must not be cited as support).
findings.proposed_fix: §3.5, replace the quoted sentence with: 'Explicit content is phenomenal only where it is in closure (§6.4). The parent theory distinguishes the active closure, between the active self and world models, which gives the sense of being here and now, from a rudimentary closure that it hypothesizes may hold among the non-active explicit models and that would mark the floor of minimal consciousness (Gruber, 2026, Sections 3.3, 3.5); explicit content in neither is preconscious, what psychology called the subconscious. Let χ_loop(s, ν, t) ∈ [0, 1] be the fraction of the activity at (s, ν) in closure at t, with the active loop as its reference case and a stated lower floor for any rudimentary-closure claim; implicit content is not preconscious but non-conscious.' §6.3 Minimal row: 'Rudimentary closure, hypothesized to hold among non-active explicit models (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.5); the self is mirrored in the world model it closes with, with no self-representation; same depth as basic, poorer content.'

findings.section: MISSING — 2.1 The Model Space (definition of 'model'); 4.1 (explicit models as projections)
findings.quote: MISSING
findings.problem: The formalization never says what a model is. §2.1 calls every point of M 'a distinct model the substrate is running' and §4.1 defines EWM(t) = Π_EWM·x(t) as a projection, so any direction of the state vector counts. The master (S366, undeposited but ruled) now defines a model by two criteria, write access (M updates so that it follows its target T) and read access (its representations can be evaluated by the system), with boundary recognition following from T rather than a third criterion, and with the rule that a model must be readable while being actually read is required only for consciousness. MG's operational rulings add: a model is recurring activity (recurrence every n steps counts; strict consecutive persistence is not required), arbitrary directions of activity are not models, world-model parts must themselves pass WRITE, and generated-not-stored is trivial and should not be inflated. Without this the ρ density, the ICA/NMF estimation of §2.6 and the w of §6.4 have no criterion for what counts as mass.
findings.evidence: Master §3.1 l.152 ('A model must be readable; that it is actually read is required only for consciousness … A structure the system cannot evaluate is a data structure, not a model'); Table 1 'Model' l.164; decisions.md D-S366-A, D-S366-D (1), D-S366-G T7; crucible decisions.md 2026-10-30 ~08:50, 2026-10-28 ~09:20; findings F01, F02, F03, F04, C03.
findings.proposed_fix: Insert at the start of §2.1, before the two axes: 'A point of M is a model in the parent theory\'s sense (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.1): a state or structure M of the system that follows a target domain T, with two criteria. Write access: M updates so that it tracks T, which on activity data means it predicts its target better than a time-shifted null. Readability: the system can evaluate M, which on activity data means the carrying pattern projects to units outside itself. T fixes the model\'s boundary; boundary recognition is a consequence, not a third criterion. That a model is actually read is required for consciousness, not for being a model. An explicit model is recurring activity meeting both criteria; it may recur after gaps rather than persist through consecutive windows, and an arbitrary direction of the state vector is not a model. Explicit models are generated from the implicit models and current input rather than stored, which in a substrate with fixed weights and short cell memory holds by construction.' In §4.1 after the projections: 'Π_EWM and Π_ESM select the patterns that meet the model criteria of Section 2.1; they are not cell masks, and a projection that passes neither criterion is not a model.'

findings.section: MISSING — 5.1 The ESM as an Input-Dependent Attractor; 2.3 The Minimum-Configuration Constraint
findings.quote: MISSING
findings.problem: The master now specifies what counts as a self model and what the realistic ESM is: a lower-dimensional, integrated model (not a 'copy') of the actual self, integrated from several implicit models plus sensory input and motor feedback, modulated by salience and memory; the simplest self model is a low-dimensional integrated model of the body or at least a viewpoint, the origin to which the senses are referred, and a position estimate alone is not one; in a simple system the explicit and implicit self models are hard to tell apart. Crucible's D10 result gives a first instance: an input-locked, integrated, WRITE-passing recurring direction (hunger + pain, at 40k; danger proximity did not replicate) in a frozen 8k creature, with no closure of any kind. The formalization has no criterion separating a self model from a position datum, nothing on the integration/viewpoint content of e(t), and no formal statement of the case 'ESM-scope mass with χ_loop = 0', which is the predicted non-conscious configuration.
findings.evidence: Master §3.4.3 l.325 ('The simplest self model is a low-dimensional, integrated model of the body, or at least a viewpoint … A position estimate alone is not one … A viewpoint differs from a position estimate'); §3.2 l.226; decisions.md D-S366-E, D-S366-H, D-S366-I; crucible docs/results/cru234-find-frozen-2026-10-30.md §3-§7, §10; findings F07, F08, F09, C04, C08, C23 (cite D10, say 'model' not 'copy', 40k content hunger + pain).
findings.proposed_fix: §5.1, after 'Let e(t) represent the aggregate ESM state …': 'e(t) is a low-dimensional, integrated model of the system itself, drawn from several implicit models together with interoceptive, proprioceptive and motor feedback and modulated by salience and memory (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.2). Self-scope mass counts toward θ_ESM in Section 2.3 only if it is integrated, at least two body variables or a viewpoint, the origin to which the senses are referred and which binds their input; a position estimate alone does not qualify (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.4.3). In a simple system e(t) and the implicit self model it is generated from are hard to tell apart, which bounds how sharply ν_crit can be estimated there (Section 4.6). The theory predicts, and the formalization must allow, self-scope mass with χ_loop = 0: an explicit self model that no world model closes with. An in-silico instance exists: in a frozen spiking creature a recurring free-cortex direction follows hunger and pain better than a time-shifted null, is integrated, and enters no closure (Gruber, 2026d, current version). It is a relay of the interoceptive signal, carries no claim to consciousness, and its readability is still to be checked.' Add to §2.3 after the four-corner constraint: 'Mass at the ESM corner is necessary; mass there without closure (Section 6.4) is the predicted non-conscious case.'

findings.section: 2.6 Cautions on Model-Space Estimation; 3.1 Transfer Entropy Formulation; 4.2 (σ, λ_max); Phase 1 Module 2; Phase 2 Module 1
findings.quote: Any implementation of the model-space framework should include criteria for distinguishing real modes from artifacts — for example, requiring that identified modes correlate with behavior, stimulus content, or report, rather than treating every ICA component as a real model.
findings.problem: Crucible's CRU-227/CRU-234 work shows the stated criterion is insufficient and names the failure modes: any rotation of a content-carrying subspace also correlates with behaviour (8-9 of 18 random-basis directions 'counted' vs 2 for ICA), fixed wiring guarantees stable shared directions with no content, the input area's rate must be the covariate, drifting targets create false negatives, and ICA lost a stationary mode in 4/7 pairs. For closure and permeability: any two projections of one recurrent substrate predict each other 100-500 ms ahead, so a circular-shift surrogate cannot see it, and a frozen random net passes a lagged-prediction closure test (the 40k lead was retracted on this ground). The paper's T_{A_s→B_s} and the §6.4 closure statistic carry no such null. The readout fallacy (master §7.3, §8.6, didactic #41) adds that ICA/NMF/RSA return the structure of the measure in part (metric, dimensionality fixed by the method), which also qualifies §2.6's 'the number of independent axes … is a quantity to be *measured*' and §2.5/§5.3's RSA-based predictions. §4.2's σ lacks the master's rate-matched surrogate requirement, and λ_max estimated from time series reads positive for a noise-driven stable linear system. Module 2's 'known "implicit" processing regions' misstates the implicit side as regions (registry #5: implicit = structure, not a region's activity).
findings.evidence: Findings C12, C13, C17, C18, F32; crucible docs/results/cru234-find-frozen-2026-10-30.md §1, §2, §4, §10-§11; cru227-p1-2026-10-28.md §6; master §3.6.1 and §8.12 ('A σ is therefore reported only beside its rate-matched surrogate'); master §7.3 l.925, §8.6 l.1023; .claude/knowledge/didactic-patterns.md #41; registry #5.
findings.proposed_fix: §2.6, replace the quoted sentence with: 'Any implementation must state its criteria in advance. Correlation with behaviour or stimulus is not enough: any rotation of a content-carrying subspace correlates too, and fixed wiring guarantees stable shared directions that carry no content. A candidate mode counts as a model when it meets the write criterion of Section 2.1 against a time-shifted null with the input area\'s activity as a covariate, when the claim survives random rotations within the same subspace or the basis is fixed before the data are seen, and when drifting targets are scored against a fold-mean baseline. Decomposition methods fix part of the structure they return, the metric and the number of dimensions among it, so the "measured" dimensionality above is the structure of the measure until shown otherwise (Gruber, 2026, Sections 7.3, 8.6).' §3.1, after the permeability definition: 'Two projections of one recurrent substrate predict each other at short lags whatever they carry, so T_{A_s→B_s} is reported against a null of random directions within the same subspaces, conditioned on common input, with a time-shift surrogate kept only as a floor; the same holds for the closure statistic of Section 6.4.' §4.2: add 'σ is reported beside a rate-matched surrogate, since a subsampled branching ratio tracks firing rate; a λ_max estimated from a driven time series is compared with a noise-driven stable linear null before it is read as chaos.' Module 2: replace 'known "implicit" processing regions and known "explicit"/"conscious access" regions' with 'substrate activity below and explicit activity above the threshold of Section 3.1, estimated at each scope position'.

findings.section: MISSING — 2.7 Locating the Engine (operational free-modelling measure); 4.5 (free modeling definition)
findings.quote: Promotion of the criterion to a prediction should wait on an operational measure of free modelling capacity that has been validated independently of the localization it is being used to perform, on pain of the circularity the cautions of Section 2.6 warn about.
findings.problem: The paper asks for an operational measure of free modelling and has none. The master now carries one as a test design (MG S355, AIW-320, v28): a novel-input probe against an unrolled feedforward model of matched capacity (same parameters, exposure and memory) trained on the system's own history, compared on novel input of increasing compositional depth, with criticality signatures recorded alongside and not as the test. The master also adds play as a behavioural marker of free modelling (v29). The formalization's definition ('open-ended computation recruited for self-modeling') differs from the master's Table 1b ('recruited by the system for its own modeling') and §6.4 ('for models that serve no present goal'); the three wordings should be reconciled, with the master's as reference. Scope: a design, not a validated measure; play is a marker, not a criterion, and its absence establishes nothing.
findings.evidence: Master Table 1b l.196 ('Novel-input probe: train an unrolled feedforward model of matched capacity …'); §6.4 l.813 (play); backlog AIW-320, AIW-347; findings F22, F25.
findings.proposed_fix: §2.7, after the quoted sentence: 'The parent theory supplies a candidate: a novel-input probe, in which an unrolled feedforward model of matched capacity, trained on the system\'s own history, is compared with the system on novel input of increasing compositional depth, criticality signatures recorded alongside and not as the test (Gruber, 2026, Table 1b). It is a design, not yet a validated measure, so the criterion stays a method until the probe has been run. In behaviour, free modelling shows as activity without an immediate payoff, play its clearest form (Gruber, 2026, Section 6.4); that is a marker, not a criterion, and its absence establishes nothing.' §4.5 conjunction: '[ free modeling: open-ended computation recruited by the system for its own modeling, including models that serve no present goal ]'. Phase 4 prediction 2: add 'measured by the novel-input probe of Section 2.7'.

findings.section: 1.2 Why Not Simply Formalize the Four Models?; 2.3; 4.6 The Implicit-Explicit Threshold as a Graph Phase Transition; 5.2 Quantitative Predictions
findings.quote: To formalize the theory correctly, therefore, requires treating the four models not as four discrete objects but as four *regions* in a continuous space of modeling activity
findings.problem: The aIware RCA of crucible's misread records that this wording, with §2.3's 'four regions R_IWM … R_ESM', invited the reading of explicit models as regions, which MG ruled a total misunderstanding of FMT: the explicit models are sustained spiking patterns, never regions, populations or modules. The abstract-space sense is legitimate but shares the word. §4.6 then characterizes explicit processing as 'low-dimensional, structured, and local', which reads as localization against the registry's rule that explicit models are non-localizable transient dynamics (only the implicit side localizes to structure), and §5.2 uses 'default mode network activity (proxy for ESM)' without the master's qualifier that DMN activity is a correlate and not a localization claim.
findings.evidence: docs/research/fmt-crucible-misread-rca.md §2; docs/sources/mg-2026-10-27-fmt-substrate-spec.md; decisions.md D-S365-B; master Table 1 'Self-simulation' ('This is a neural correlate, not a localization claim') and §3.2 l.209; registry fmt-misconception-registry.md #5 (MG: 'the explicit ones are NOT localizable'); findings F05, C01.
findings.proposed_fix: §1.2: 'as four corners of an abstract scope-mode space, neighbourhoods in a coordinate system of modeling activity and not regions of tissue'. §2.3: 'define four neighbourhoods N_IWM … N_ESM of the four corners' (rename R_k to N_k throughout). Add one sentence at the end of §2.1: 'Nothing in this space is a location in the brain: implicit models are stored in structure and can be localized, explicit models are distributed activity and cannot (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.2).' §4.6: replace 'low-dimensional, structured, and local (explicit)' with 'low-dimensional and structured (explicit), distributed across the substrate rather than confined to a region'. §5.2: 'default mode network activity (a correlate of ESM activity, not its location)'.

findings.section: MISSING — 2.1 The Model Space (kind of explicit model); 2.6 Emergent dimensionality
findings.quote: MISSING
findings.problem: MG's 2026-10-27 spec (unhedged) distinguishes two sorts of explicit model, robust sustained patterns (what the body does and senses) and flexible dynamical patterns (prospective planning, simulation), and his D21 ruling (unhedged) separates sensory-near world models, which track reality, from abstract world models. D-S366-C/E add that an input-locked pattern counts as a simple robust explicit model and that beating an input filter is a kind question, not a model criterion, so 'explicit' cannot be defined by independence from input. The (s, ν, ℓ) space has no coordinate for this, and the paper's reader would place input-locked activity on the implicit side. Scope: the robust/dynamical names come from MG's spec; crucible's merged definition ('robust lives only while the input lasts') is not MG-approved as a whole, and the regional locations MG gave are hedged guesses; Principle 2's 'survive their own inputs' is an open item (T5, CRU-238).
findings.evidence: docs/sources/mg-2026-10-27-fmt-substrate-spec.md; crucible decisions.md 2026-10-30 D21 (l.21-37); decisions.md D-S366-C, D-S366-E, D-S366-G T5; crucible docs/fmt-core.md 'Robust vs dynamical'; findings F05, F06, F16, F44, C10, C21.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §2.1 after the mode axis: 'Explicit models come in two kinds that the mode coordinate does not separate: patterns locked to current input, which carry what the body does and senses, and dynamical patterns with internal onset, which carry absent or future states (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.2; the world-model side of this is the contrast between sensory-near models that track reality and abstract models). An input-locked pattern that meets the model criteria is an explicit model; whether a pattern outlives its input is a question about its kind, not about whether it is a model. The formalization treats kind as a label on each model, not as a further axis, until a measure for it exists.' Do not adopt Principle 2's 'survive their own inputs' clause anywhere; §1.1 correctly omits it and should keep doing so until T5 is ruled.

findings.section: 2.5 Connection to Principal Bundle Geometry; 6.2 The Observability Constraint; 7.4 Forking as Coproduct
findings.quote: with only one active at any given time.
findings.problem: The master (T3) now reserves 'active' for the active self model and active world model, the parts in closure, and changes other uses to 'running'. The formalization uses the old sense three times: §2.5 'the EWM is the active representation', §6.2 'the EWM actively models', §7.4 'only one active at any given time'. Under the new sense §7.4 would say that only one alter is in the closed loop, which is a different claim from the one intended (one alter running the simulation).
findings.evidence: decisions.md D-S366-G T3; master Table 4 l.709 ('All four running'); finding F11.
findings.proposed_fix: §2.5: 'the EWM is the running representation (the encoder\'s output)'. §6.2: 'the set of states, properties, and processes that the EWM represents'. §7.4: 'with only one running the simulation at any given time'. Reserve 'active' for e_a and w_a of §6.4.

findings.section: 4.7 The Two Dimensions of Criticality (Orthogonality paragraph)
findings.quote: The *route* out is phase- and scale-dependent and is not settled — onset and spread are heterogeneous and often desynchronized at single-neuron scale, while hypersynchrony dominates the late phase and termination — so the case should be stated route-agnostically as exit from Class 4 rather than as a specific departure direction.
findings.problem: The master (AIW-340, v29) now reports direct human evidence for generalized seizures: in the generalized seizures measured so far (two intracranial, one MEG) the slow cortical electrodynamics crossed the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022), the hypersynchrony route; focal seizures lose power-law statistics (Meisel et al., 2012) with heterogeneous onset (Truccolo et al., 2011). The route-robust framing can stay, but 'not settled' now omits the evidence and the didactic 'Cautions' item it rests on predates it. Scope: n = 3 generalized seizures, slow electrodynamics only; focal onset remains heterogeneous.
findings.evidence: Master §3.7 l.501, §10.3 l.1158; backlog AIW-340; finding F20.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'The route out differs by seizure type and phase: focal ictal recordings lose the power-law statistics of the critical regime (Meisel et al., 2012) with heterogeneous single-neuron activity at onset (Truccolo et al., 2011), and in the generalized seizures measured so far, two intracranial and one MEG, the slow cortical electrodynamics crossed the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022). The decomposition needs only the exit from Class 4, whichever route obtains.' Add Meisel et al. (2012) and Truccolo et al. (2011) to the references if cited.

findings.quote: and phenomenology is a real, physical effect on that level, arising exactly where the modelling closes on itself.
findings.problem: The master states Principle 3 as an identity, 'phenomenality is closure … The principle is an identity, not a law connecting two things', and the paper's own §6.1 and §9.2 treat closure as constitutive. 'A real, physical effect … arising where' reads as a law connecting two things, the reading the master excludes. (The master wording predates the S342 baseline, so this was missed in the last update rather than newly introduced.)
findings.evidence: Master §3 l.139 ('phenomenality is closure. This is the theory\'s single bridging commitment'); master commit 7d23a2f7 (2026-10-17).
findings.proposed_fix: 'and phenomenology is real and physical, and is that level\'s modelling closed on itself, an identity rather than a law connecting two things (Gruber, 2026, Section 3).'

findings.section: 3.2 Permeability Profiles as Quantitative Predictions (Table 1, Salvia row); 5.1
findings.quote: | Salvia divinorum (high dose) | High + ESM disruption | Self-scope P collapses | $T_{\mathrm{ISM} \to \mathrm{ESM}} \to 0$; $T_{\mathrm{IWM} \to \mathrm{ESM}}$ ↑ |
findings.problem: Since S349 the prediction runs inside a dose window: at the highest doses salvinorin A gates external audiovisual input (Maqueda et al., 2015) and identity content is predicted to draw on internal imagery. §5.2 states the window; the table row says 'high dose' with T_IWM→ESM rising, which at the gating dose is the opposite of what the master predicts for external content. The row should name the range it means. Also, §5.1's 'The ESM has a stable attractor basin' should admit recurrence after gaps (MG: a pattern 'may re-occur every n steps').
findings.evidence: Master §8.3 l.987 ('external audiovisual input is gated in a dose-dependent way'); decisions.md S349 (l.707); .claude/knowledge/prediction-framing.md l.58; crucible decisions.md 2026-10-28 ~09:20; findings F38, F04.
findings.proposed_fix: Row label: 'Salvia divinorum (ego-dissolving dose below audiovisual gating)'; add a table note: 'At the highest doses external input is gated and T_IWM→ESM is predicted to be carried by internally generated content.' §5.1: 'The ESM has a stable attractor basin around the "normal self" configuration, which the trajectory may leave and re-enter; recurrence, not uninterrupted persistence, is what the theory requires of an explicit model (Section 2.1).'

findings.section: MISSING — 6.5 Complexity Cost of Self-Reference; Phase 4 predictions
findings.quote: MISSING
findings.problem: The master (v29) adds the running cost of closure, the VM tax: the closed loop adds latency and loses on fast reactive work, pays on counterfactual reasoning, long-horizon planning, extrapolation and optimising over a model, and predicts that capability scales with the internal simulation budget when closure is in place and stops scaling when closure is ablated. §6.5 formalizes only capacity overhead, not time cost, and Phase 4 has no budget-scaling prediction. Scope: a price, not a barrier; the scaling claim is an untested prediction.
findings.evidence: Master §4.2.4 l.623; backlog AIW-347; finding F26; .claude/knowledge/didactic-patterns.md 'Cautions' (price, never barrier).
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §6.5: 'Closure also costs time. The loop is a simulation layer and runs slower than the substrate beneath it, so on reactive work it adds latency; the parent theory predicts that on tasks where reactive performance has plateaued and the payoff lies at a long horizon, performance rises with the simulation budget b, the time the system runs its model before acting, when closure is in place, and is flat in b when closure is ablated (Gruber, 2026, Section 4.2.4). Formally, ∂perf/∂b > 0 with closure and ≈ 0 without, at matched capacity; this is a price, not a barrier, and untested.' Add it as prediction 4 in Phase 4.

findings.section: MISSING — 3.3 The Selection Operator; 3.5 Total Conscious Content
findings.quote: MISSING
findings.problem: The master's §3.6.1 now identifies the working model (channel occupancy) with the active part of the explicit models, calls attention selection into the channel and closure the pass back over what the channel holds, and derives working-memory capacity as the channel's rank. The formalization has no channel, rank or working-model object, so the selection family G is not tied to the channel and χ_loop has no capacity bound. A caveat from the collector: the master's Sperling reading (all twelve letters accessed) sits uneasily with a rank-4 item bound, so the bound should be stated as the master states it, a rank, without choosing between item count and dimensionality. Crucible's anatomical reading (one low-rank thalamocortical channel plus a basal-ganglia-like selector) is a build target, not a theory claim.
findings.evidence: Master §3.6.1 l.436-446 ('*is* the rank of the channel'; 'The working model is the active part of the explicit models … Attention is selection *into* the channel; closure is the pass back *over* what the channel holds'); §3.4.6 l.393; findings F13, F18, C02.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §3.3: 'The parent theory locates selection on a read/write path of rank k between the implicit models and the explicit ones (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.6.1). The selection family G then specifies what enters that path, and the active parts e_a, w_a of Section 6.4 are what occupies it. The master identifies working-memory capacity with k; whether k bounds the number of items in χ_loop or the dimensionality of the content is left open here, since the master\'s own reading of partial-report data (Section 3.4.6) places more items in the loop than a rank-4 item bound allows.'

findings.section: 6.3 Self-Referential Depth via Recursive Representation (levels table, Basic row)
findings.quote: | Basic consciousness | μ₀ | ESM represents the EWM |
findings.problem: Closure in the master is mutual ('the self-model and the world model enter each other\'s update rules'); 'ESM represents the EWM' is one-directional and describes an ESM that has a world model as content, which is not closure. With E11-E13 the master locates consciousness in the mutual update, and the floor is described as the self mirrored in the world model it closes with.
findings.evidence: Master l.137-139 (Principle 3), l.893 (E12: 'closure counts only where the self-model and the world model enter each other\'s update rules'), §3.5 l.401 (H2); findings F11, F15, F17.
findings.proposed_fix: Basic row: 'ESM and EWM enter each other\'s update; the self is mirrored in the world model without taking itself as an object'. Simply extended: 'the ESM additionally represents itself in that closure'. Keep the rest.

findings.section: 4.7 Processing volume and subjective duration; 6.4 (last paragraph)
findings.quote: The function Ψ runs on the substrate; the fixed point m\* is a property of the dynamics, not of any particular substrate element.
findings.problem: The master now states that FMT takes no stance on whether a complete stored record of a run has the experience the run has, and defines 'actually perform' as the realized dependency of a trajectory with no condition on unfolding in time (SUFF-19). 'Runs on the substrate' and §4.7's processing volume per physical clock-second lean toward the unfolding view without saying so; a reply drafted for Mallavarapu & Percy also treats every FMT constituent as a present-state fact. A one-sentence gloss keeps the formalization neutral. Scope: conditional reply only if that preprint is peer-reviewed; the master's no-stance is the authority.
findings.evidence: Master §3.4.5 l.383; §3.7.3 l.537; decisions.md l.682 (SUFF-19), l.735 (S354); findings F28, F34.
findings.proposed_fix: Append to §6.4: 'Here "runs" names the realized dependency of the trajectory\'s states on one another and nothing about how the process unfolds in time; the theory takes no stance on whether a complete stored record of the trajectory shares its experience (Gruber, 2026, Sections 3.4.5, 3.7.3). The processing volume of Section 4.7 relates experienced to external duration and is neutral between the two readings.' Covered also in theory-6's replacement text if that is adopted.

reviewed.notes: Verdict: the formalization is out of line with the FMT master at HEAD on its two load-bearing formal objects, closure (§6.4, stationary fixed point over the whole explicit state vs the master's mutual updating of the active self and world models) and criticality (§4.2-4.5, a single Wolfram-class mapping that Toker 2022's two diverging axes falsify), and it still treats the ESM as an ablatable unit and cites the companion as 'validation' after several of its results were withdrawn. It is already compliant on: transformation (never dissolution) of the Hard Problem, 'selection' not 'gating', 'fully explicit' with no '(phenomenal)' on the mode axis, Hengen & Shew = 143, Prediction 2 salience/dose window in §5.1-5.2, 'preconscious' for out-of-loop explicit content, criticality as signature with L1/L2 open, graded/price framing of Prediction 1, and the generated-not-stored sentence in §6.2.
