missed.evidence: fmt-formalization.md l.166-172 (§3.1 A_s), l.191 (REM row 'T from parameters high'), l.269-272 (§4.1), l.351 (§4.6 'processing is distributed'), l.571 (Module 2); master l.164 (Table 1 Model, mode), l.196 (Implicit integrity), l.256 ('the substrate generates and sustains them').
missed.proposed_fix: §4.1: 'The implicit models are stored in W and evaluated by substrate processing: activity below ν_crit that runs through the stored structure without being generated as a model (Gruber, 2026, Table 1). The implicit side therefore has two layers, the slow parameters W (the topological level ℓ = 4 of Section 2.4) and the sub-threshold processing that evaluates them; A_s(t) of Section 3.1 is the second, which is what makes it a time-varying signal. The explicit models are patterns of activity above ν_crit, projections of the state vector.' Table 1 REM row: 'Internally driven (substrate processing through W, not s(t))' and 'T from sub-threshold processing high; T from sensory input ≈ 0'. Module 2 per theory-11.

missed.section: 6.4 Self-Referential Closure as a Fixed Point (opening) vs 4.5 The Two Thresholds as a Conjunction
missed.quote: The most compact formalization: consciousness occurs when the coupled update of self-model and world-model reaches a **fixed point**.
missed.problem: 'Consciousness occurs when' states closure as sufficient, while §4.5 declares that 'This paper formalizes only the two necessary thresholds' and cites the master's sufficient conjunction (four model kinds under closure, free modeling, embodiment, a pain-pleasure axis; master l.531). The two sections contradict each other on the paper's own scope, and §6.4's version also omits the free-modeling requirement of §4.5.
missed.evidence: fmt-formalization.md l.343 (§4.5 last paragraph), l.495 (§6.4); master §3.7.3 l.531.
missed.proposed_fix: Replace 'consciousness occurs when' with 'self-referential closure, the third principle's necessary condition, holds when', and add at the end of §6.4: 'Closure is one of the two necessary thresholds of Section 4.5; the parent theory's sufficient condition is the conjunction stated there.' (Subsumed by theory-1's corrected fix if that is adopted.)

findings.section: §4.2 Three Candidate Criticality Measures / §4.3 Disambiguating Criticality Types / §4.5 The Two Thresholds as a Conjunction
findings.quote: σ < 1: subcritical (activity dies out) → Wolfram Class 1/2 [...] σ > 1: supercritical (activity explodes) → Wolfram Class 3 [...] (e.g., deep propofol anesthesia, where cortical dynamics also turn subcritical) [...] Empirical resolution: compare PCI (or another consciousness-tracking measure) against σ and λ_max independently, particularly in states where the two measures diverge.
findings.problem: The paper maps σ and λ_max onto the same Wolfram class labels as if they agreed, treats the divergent case as a future hypothetical, and calls propofol simply 'subcritical'. The master (HEAD) records measured divergence: waking cortex is slightly subcritical by branching ratio (Priesemann 2014) and slightly chaotic by slow electrodynamics (Toker et al. 2022); propofol is forced subcritical on the branching axis and deeper into the chaotic phase on the edge-of-chaos axis. Under the paper's labels propofol is Class 1/2 by σ and Class 3 by λ at once, so the two mappings contradict each other on a measured state, and §4.5's 'turn subcritical' holds on one axis only. Toker et al. (2022) is not cited in the formalization although the master uses it in Table 4, §5.3, §8.1, §3.7 and §10.3.
findings.evidence: Master paper/full/four-model-theory-full.md l.711 (Table 4 propofol row), l.718 (column note), l.720 (§5.3), l.959 (§8.1); finding F19; master reference l.1916: Toker, D., et al. (2022). Consciousness is supported by near-critical slow cortical electrodynamics. PNAS, 119(7), e2024455119.
findings.proposed_fix: §4.2: replace the single class ladder with per-axis labels and add the measured case: 'σ and λ_max index different transitions (§4.3), and in human cortex they now point different ways: waking cortex is slightly subcritical by its branching ratio (Priesemann et al., 2014) and slightly chaotic by its slow electrodynamics (Toker et al., 2022); under propofol the branching ratio falls further below one while the slow electrodynamics move deeper into the chaotic phase (Toker et al., 2022).' §4.3 'Empirical resolution': replace 'particularly in states where the two measures diverge' with 'waking and propofol anesthesia are already such states (Toker et al., 2022), so the comparison can begin with them'. §4.5: 'deep propofol anesthesia, where the branching ratio turns subcritical while the slow electrodynamics move deeper into chaos (Toker et al., 2022)'. Add Toker et al. (2022) to the reference list.

findings.quote: Computational validation is reported in the companion (Gruber, 2026d); the specification below does not depend on those results.
findings.problem: 'Validation is reported' overstates the companion. The companion itself frames every result as 'mechanism demonstrations at toy, reservoir, or gridworld scale' and says 'the scaled test of the central dependency is not attempted here'. None of the three Phase 4 predictions has been tested as stated: prediction 3 (EWM coverage ablation) has no companion result at all; prediction 2 rests on shallow memory-bound reservoir tasks only; prediction 1's ablation uses a gridworld agent whose ESM is a module object, which MG's 2026-10-27 ruling (explicit models are activity, never regions or modules) leaves as an open question. The companion's record also carries items now at risk or withdrawn: the §6 re-entry null is AT RISK and not re-run, A#1 'closure maintains a model' is withdrawn, the region-labelled ClosureBrain results are no longer FMT evidence, A#6 survives only as slow-reservoir memory, and no FlowBody-based result is quotable (CRU-222).
findings.evidence: drafts/companion-computational-paper-draft.md l.77, l.250-252; docs/research/aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md (verdict, rows 2, 3, 16, 18, 19, open questions 1-3); .claude/knowledge/prediction-framing.md S362 correction; ~/crucible/docs/cru226-juelich-substance.md §4 items 1, 3, 6, 7; findings F23, F24, C18, C20.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'The companion (Gruber, 2026d) reports mechanism demonstrations at toy, reservoir and gridworld scale; none of the three predictions below has been tested as stated there, the gridworld agent implements its self-model as a module rather than as emergent activity, and parts of that record are under re-analysis. The specification below does not depend on those results.' Make the same change in §10 ('Computational validation is reported in the companion').

findings.quote: the spectral radius tunes the substrate's open-ended computational capability, and the edge is not where that capability peaks (Section 4.4)
findings.problem: The only reservoir result behind this sentence (CRU-203, cited in §4.4 as the thirty-reservoir replication) measured a lag-6 operand-memory peak on shallow, memory-bound tasks. No open-ended capability was measured in any rate reservoir, and crucible retitled the ledger row to 'a dissociation, not support'. The master is careful on this point: 'in echo-state networks memory and computation co-peak in the driven-stable, ordered regime' and 'whether free modeling at depth needs a near-critical operating point in any substrate is open; no task deep enough to test it has yet been built'. The formalization's sentence places the open-ended capability optimum where only a shallow-task optimum was found.
findings.evidence: Master l.456 (§3.7 'The requirement is specific'); ~/crucible/docs/results/fmt-evidence-ledger.md row 2 (commit 08222cb); docs/research/aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md Q19 ('No open-ended capability was measured in any rate reservoir'); finding C19.
findings.proposed_fix: 'the spectral radius tunes where the substrate's performance peaks; on the shallow, memory-bound tasks measured so far that peak lies in the driven-stable, ordered regime rather than at the edge (Section 4.4), and whether open-ended free modeling at depth needs a near-critical operating point is untested.'

findings.section: §4.6 The Implicit-Explicit Threshold as a Graph Phase Transition / §6.6 Renormalization Group Fixed Point / §9.1 Bridge to physics
findings.quote: If the consciousness-cosmology structural identity proposed by the companion cosmological model (Gruber, 2026c) is correct [...] would be the same mathematical object — an RG fixed point — at different scales. This is the consciousness-cosmology structural identity expressed in the language of renormalization. [...] The companion cosmological model (Gruber, 2026c) proposes a structural identity
findings.problem: The attribution is circular and now inaccurate. The cosmology paper no longer proposes the identity: it states 'Whether this rises to a strict structural identity — rather than a strong correspondence — is left open, and is the burden of the formalization', and it limits the correspondence to the implicit/explicit axis with no counterpart for the world/self axis. Each paper therefore attributes the identity claim to the other. Two further scope limits are omitted: Wetterich's automaton-QFT equivalence is proved for reversible automata and the cosmology paper's §8.4 now rests on reversibility only along the realised trajectory (AIW-334, unchecked), while the cortical automaton is dissipative; and §6.6's 'same mathematical object' asserts what both papers elsewhere call open.
findings.evidence: paper/cosmology/sb-hc4a.md l.499 ('is left open, and is the burden of the formalization'), l.519 ('The correspondence covers one axis [...] It has no counterpart for the world/self axis'), l.559 (reversibility commitment); backlog AIW-334 (finding F43).
findings.proposed_fix: §4.6: 'If the consciousness-cosmology correspondence of the companion cosmological model (Gruber, 2026c), which that paper limits to the implicit/explicit axis and leaves open as to whether it is an identity, holds, then ...'. §6.6 last paragraph: 'The connection to the companion cosmology (Gruber, 2026c) is the conjecture this program is asked to decide: the cosmological fixed point Ψ(U) = U and the consciousness fixed point Ψ(m*) = m* may be instances of one mathematical object, an RG fixed point, at different scales. Gruber (2026c) states the correspondence for the implicit/explicit axis only and leaves identity open; Wetterich's equivalence holds for reversible automata, and the cortical automaton is dissipative, so the QFT dual assumed above is a further conjecture.' §9.1: 'proposes a structural correspondence, limited to the implicit/explicit axis, and leaves open whether it is an identity'.

findings.quote: Compute transfer entropy between neural signals in known "implicit" processing regions and known "explicit"/"conscious access" regions across existing neuroimaging datasets [...] "Transfer entropy from implicit to explicit regions increases by factor k at dose d"
findings.problem: The operationalization assigns implicit and explicit models to different brain regions. On the theory's own definitions implicit models are stored in connectivity and explicit models are activity patterns, in the same tissue (master Table 1), and MG ruled on 2026-10-27 that explicit models 'ARE NOT REGIONS IN A NETWORK'. The paper's own §3.1 defines permeability without regions, as information flow between the below- and above-threshold mass at one scope position. Module 2 and §9.1 therefore describe a measurement that cannot test the quantity §3.1 defines.
findings.evidence: Master l.170-172 (Table 1 'Implicit model' = connectivity; 'Explicit model' = generated activity patterns); docs/sources/mg-2026-10-27-fmt-substrate-spec.md; docs/research/fmt-crucible-misread-rca.md §2; findings F05, C01; formalization §3.1 (A_s, B_s defined as mass splits at ν_crit).
findings.proposed_fix: Module 2: 'Compute transfer entropy from the implicit-mode signal A_s to the explicit-mode signal B_s of §3.1, estimated from the same recordings (the implicit and explicit models share tissue and differ in mode, not location), across existing neuroimaging datasets ...'. §9.1: '"Transfer entropy from the implicit to the explicit mode increases by factor k at dose d"'.

findings.quote: These predictions are directly testable with existing neuroimaging data — transfer entropy can be estimated from EEG, MEG, and fMRI time series [...] | Deep sleep (NREM) | Very low | Uniform suppression | Near-zero transfer entropy |
findings.problem: Two defects. (a) No null is specified. Crucible measured that lagged prediction between any two projections of one recurrent substrate is generically non-zero and that a circular-shift surrogate cannot see this (a frozen random recurrent net passed the test), so a raw T from A_s to B_s reads coupling as permeability, and 'near-zero transfer entropy' in NREM is not what a recurrent cortex will show. (b) 'Directly testable' conflicts with §3.1's own statement that estimating A_s and B_s 'is a separate problem' to which the §2.6 cautions apply in full; the predictions are testable only after a ρ estimator exists.
findings.evidence: ~/crucible/docs/results/cru234-find-frozen-2026-10-30.md §10-§11 (retracted 40k 'weak closure', basis dependence, common-input confound); finding C12; formalization §3.1 l.174.
findings.proposed_fix: After the permeability equation add: 'Two projections of one recurrent substrate predict each other at short lags whatever their content, so T must be reported against a null that destroys only the implicit-to-explicit coupling: condition on shared input and compare against random rotations of the explicit-mode basis, with a time-shift surrogate as a floor.' Table 1 NREM row: 'At the null floor'. Replace 'directly testable with existing neuroimaging data' with 'testable on existing EEG, MEG and fMRI datasets once A_s and B_s can be estimated (§2.6)'.

findings.quote: for example, requiring that identified modes correlate with behavior, stimulus content, or report, rather than treating every ICA component as a real model [...] the number of independent axes in the model space is a quantity to be measured, not assumed.
findings.problem: The one criterion offered for separating real modes from artifacts is insufficient by measurement: any rotation of a content-carrying subspace also correlates with behavior or stimulus, and in crucible random rotations of the ICA basis produced 8-9 of 18 'counting' directions against 2 for ICA, so the stated rule would have fired under a random basis. A pattern claim needs a rotation-invariant subspace test or a basis criterion fixed in advance. The 'to be measured' sentence also omits the master's readout-fallacy caveat that the method fixes part of the structure it returns, the metric and the number of dimensions among it.
findings.evidence: ~/crucible/docs/results/cru227-p1-2026-10-28.md §6; cru234-find-frozen-2026-10-30.md §1-§4 (finding C13); master l.925 (§7.3 readout fallacy), l.1023 (§8.6); .claude/knowledge/didactic-patterns.md #41 (finding F32).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the example with: 'for example, requiring that an identified mode follows a stated target better than a time-shifted null, with the input area's activity as covariate, and that the claim survive random rotations of the basis within the same shared subspace; correlation with behavior alone does not suffice, since any rotation of a content-carrying subspace correlates too.' After 'to be measured, not assumed' add: 'with the caveat that the decomposition method fixes part of what it returns, the metric and the number of dimensions among it (Gruber, 2026, Section 7.3).'

findings.section: §5.1 The ESM as an Input-Dependent Attractor / §5.2 Quantitative Predictions / §3.2 Table 1 (Salvia row)
findings.quote: I(e; i_ext): How much the ESM state correlates with external sensory input. [...] Ego dissolution: I(e; i_self) → 0; I(e; i_ext) → I_max. The ESM identity tracks the most salient external content. [...] | Salvia divinorum (high dose) | High + ESM disruption | Self-scope P collapses | T_ISM→ESM → 0; T_IWM→ESM ↑ |
findings.problem: Prediction 2 is aligned with the master in substance (salience, salvinorin A, heartbeat split, dose window), but the dose logic is internally inconsistent. §5.1 defines i_ext as 'the most salient content in the explicit world-model'; §5.2 redefines it as 'external sensory input', then predicts I(e; i_ext) → I_max at ego dissolution while also stating that at the highest doses external input no longer reaches the subject. The master runs the tests below the gating range and predicts identity content from internally generated imagery at the highest doses. Table 1's 'Salvia divinorum (high dose)' row does not say which dose range it means, although the master's test and its own §5.2 window exclude the highest doses.
findings.evidence: Master l.987 (§8.3: 'the tests run at doses below the gating range. At the highest doses the account predicts identity content drawn from internally generated imagery'); master reference l.1668 (Maqueda et al., 2015); docs/decisions.md S349 entry; findings F38, F10.
findings.proposed_fix: §5.2 bullet: 'I(e; i_ext): How much the ESM state correlates with the most salient content of the explicit world-model, external or internally generated.' Ego-dissolution bullet: 'Ego dissolution, inside the dose window: I(e; i_self) → 0; I(e; i_ext) → I_max, with i_ext external while external input still reaches the subject and internally generated above the gating dose (Maqueda et al., 2015).' Table 1 row label: 'Salvinorin A (ego-dissolution dose, below external-input gating)'. Add Maqueda et al. (2015) to the reference list.

findings.quote: The route out is phase- and scale-dependent and is not settled — onset and spread are heterogeneous and often desynchronized at single-neuron scale, while hypersynchrony dominates the late phase and termination — so the case should be stated route-agnostically as exit from Class 4 rather than as a specific departure direction.
findings.problem: Stale relative to the master, which since AIW-340 states direct human evidence for both seizure types: focal ictal recordings lose power-law statistics (Meisel et al., 2012) and in the generalized seizures measured so far (two intracranial, one MEG) the slow cortical electrodynamics crossed the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022). The route-agnostic statement of E ≈ 0 can stand, but 'is not settled' omits the evidence and its small n.
findings.proposed_fix: 'The route out differs by phase and scale and the decomposition does not depend on it: focal ictal recordings lose the power-law statistics of the critical regime (Meisel et al., 2012), and in the three generalized seizures measured so far the slow cortical electrodynamics crossed the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022), while onset is heterogeneous at single-neuron scale. The case is therefore stated as exit from Class 4 by whichever route obtains.' Add Meisel et al. (2012) and Toker et al. (2022) to the references.

findings.quote: The branching ratio σ and Lyapunov exponent λ_max are already measured in the ConCrit literature (Algom & Shriki, 2026; Hengen & Shew, 2025).
findings.problem: Hengen and Shew's 143-dataset synthesis and ConCrit concern avalanche and branching statistics. The Lyapunov-exponent measurements across conscious states (waking, propofol, LSD, seizure) are Toker et al. (2022), which the formalization does not cite.
findings.evidence: Master l.711-718 (Table 4 edge-of-chaos entries all cite Toker et al., 2022); master l.1524 (Hengen & Shew, Neuron 113(16), 2582-2598).
findings.proposed_fix: 'The branching ratio σ is already measured across states in the avalanche literature (Hengen & Shew, 2025; Algom & Shriki, 2026), and the edge-of-chaos coordinate across waking, propofol, LSD and generalized seizure by Toker et al. (2022).'

findings.quote: σ_low ≈ 0.95 and σ_high ≈ 1.1 (slightly subcritical to slightly supercritical, consistent with Priesemann et al., 2013, 2014)
findings.problem: Priesemann et al. report a slightly subcritical waking state (σ ≈ 0.98); neither paper supports a supercritical upper bound, so 'consistent with' covers only the lower half of the band. MG also ruled (D-S360-3) that state profiles be drawn as regions, which the band does, but the upper end needs its own source or a statement that it is the paper's own margin.
findings.evidence: Master l.470 ('σ ≈ 0.98 — slightly subcritical'); master Table 1 'Criticality' row; docs/decisions.md l.772 (D-S360-3); docs/reference-manifest.json fmt_formal:Priesemann2014 title 'driven, slightly subcritical brain state'.
findings.proposed_fix: '(the lower end consistent with the slightly subcritical waking values of Priesemann et al., 2013, 2014; the upper end is this paper's margin for transient supercritical excursions and has no measured anchor)'.

findings.section: §5.2 Quantitative Predictions / §5.3 The Density Migration Account
findings.quote: measure the correlation between default mode network activity (proxy for ESM) and controlled sensory input versus interoceptive input across dose levels.
findings.problem: The master declines this identification: 'The theory does not identify self-simulation with DMN activity specifically ... best understood as a candidate correlate rather than a definitive signature', and Prediction 4 states the DMN mapping is empirical, 'not derived from FMT's architecture'. 'Proxy for ESM' also carries the region reading MG ruled out on 2026-10-27.
findings.evidence: Master l.166, l.184 (Table 1 note c), l.1007 (§8.5); findings F05, C01.
findings.proposed_fix: 'measure the correlation between activity in the networks that are candidate correlates of self-referential processing (default mode structures; Gruber, 2026, Table 1 note c, a correlate and not a localization of the ESM) and controlled sensory input versus interoceptive input across dose levels.'

findings.quote: each constituting a distinct experiential self, with only one active at any given time.
findings.problem: The master says alters 'alternate in controlling the simulation' and makes no exclusivity claim; co-conscious alters are reported in the DID literature, so 'only one active at any given time' is an empirical claim stronger than the parent's. 'Active' is also now a reserved term in the master (the active self and world models whose mutual updating is the closed loop, §3.3).
findings.evidence: Master l.787 (§6.2 DID), l.256 (§3.3 active parts); finding F11 (T3: 'active' reserved, other uses become 'running').
findings.proposed_fix: 'each constituting a distinct experiential self, alternating in control of the simulation (Gruber, 2026, Section 6.2).'

findings.quote: It also provides a formal account of why the six-layer neocortex exceeds the three-layer minimum for universal function approximation (Cybenko, 1989): the additional layers provide the overhead needed for recursive self-simulation (Gruber, 2015).
findings.problem: Cybenko's theorem concerns feedforward networks with one hidden layer; cortical laminae are not feedforward processing layers, so the comparison is a category slip and Cybenko does not support it. The master states the opposite emphasis: 'The six-layer mammalian neocortex is an evolutionary implementation of the four-model architecture, not a requirement for it', and MG has called six layers 'evolution's contingent solution'. The master carries no Cybenko-based layer-count argument, so the 2015 attribution is unverified here.
findings.evidence: Master l.649 (§4.4); docs/conversation-log.md l.785; formalization reference Cybenko (1989).
findings.proposed_fix: Either drop the sentence or hedge it: 'Whether the six-layer neocortex pays part of this overhead in its laminar structure is a question the 2015 monograph raised (Gruber, 2015); the master treats the six layers as evolution's contingent implementation, not a requirement, and Cybenko's (1989) one-hidden-layer result concerns feedforward depth, not cortical laminae.'

findings.quote: | REM dreaming | Medium | Internally driven (from W, not from s(t)) | T from parameters high; T from sensory input ≈ 0 |
findings.problem: Transfer entropy is defined over time series; W is static on the timescale of a recording, so 'T from parameters' names a measurement that cannot be taken. The master's REM row says 'EWM/ESM primarily on internal input', which is measurable as flow from implicit-mode activity.
findings.evidence: Formalization §3.1 (T defined over x_t, y_t); master l.709 (Table 4 REM row).
findings.proposed_fix: '| REM dreaming | Medium | Internally driven (from implicit-mode activity, not from s(t)) | T from A_s to B_s high; T from sensory input ≈ 0 |'

findings.section: References / in-text citations of the author's own papers
findings.quote: Gruber, M. (2026). The Four-Model Theory of Consciousness [...] Gruber, M. (2026c). Emergent spacetime [...] Gruber, M. (2026d). In-silico tests
findings.problem: Three same-year self-citations carry letters 2026, 2026c and 2026d with no 2026a or 2026b, which APA does not allow and which collides across the corpus: the master cites this formalization as 'Gruber, 2026b' and the cosmology paper cites it as 'Gruber, 2026d, §6', the letter this paper gives the in-silico companion. A reader following the cosmology paper's pointer lands on the wrong paper. ABOUT.md also still lists the formalization as 'v5' while v6 is deposited.
findings.evidence: Master l.1156 ('Gruber, 2026b'); paper/cosmology/sb-hc4a.md l.499 ('Gruber, 2026d, §6'); ABOUT.md l.29; backlog AIW-303 (v6 = 10.5281/zenodo.23483510).
findings.proposed_fix: Use one letter scheme across the four papers (2026a master, 2026b formalization, 2026c cosmology, 2026d in-silico companion): change every 'Gruber, 2026' / 'Gruber (2026)' for the master to '2026a' in text and list, and ask the cosmology paper to change its '2026d, §6' pointer to '2026b, §6'. Also fix the edited-volume entry: 'Wibral, M., Vicente, R., & Lizier, J. T. (Eds.). (2014). Directed Information Measures in Neuroscience. Springer.'

findings.quote: The Meta-Problem becomes deductive. The system's inability to explain its own phenomenality is not a contingent limitation but a structural consequence [...] The observability constraint says this is architecturally impossible for self-referentially closed systems.
findings.problem: Stated as established what the master labels unproven and single-sided. The master's reply to Chalmers' master argument says the claim that the phenomenal gap is the indexical gap of a closed self-modeling system 'is not proven here', and §3.8 gives the meta-problem two mechanisms (structural opacity plus occasional leaks through the boundary), the second of which the formalization locates in D (§3.4) but omits from consequence 1.
findings.evidence: Master l.629 (§4.2.5 'that claim is not proven here'), l.545-549 (§3.8 opacity and leaks); findings F36, F37.
findings.proposed_fix: Consequence 1: 'The Meta-Problem acquires a structural source. On the constitutive reading the parent theory adopts but does not prove (Gruber, 2026, Section 4.2.5), the system's inability to explain its own phenomenality follows from O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM; the leaks the parent theory adds as a second mechanism (Section 3.8) enter here through the diffusion term D of §3.4.' Consequence 2: replace 'architecturally impossible' with 'architecturally excluded on that reading'.

findings.quote: Explicit content is phenomenal only where it enters the closed loop of self-model and world-model (§6.4); explicit content held outside that loop is preconscious (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.4.6).
findings.problem: The master (HEAD, undeposited) now carries MG's hedged hypothesis that minimal consciousness 'can arise among non-active explicit models, without the active closure that gives the full sense of being here and now'. The citation to §3.4.6 remains accurate, but with χ_loop binary (in or out of one loop) C(t), which the paper predicts to correlate with PCI, cannot represent a rudimentary closure outside the active loop. The hypothesis is hedged (MG: 'may'), so the fix is a graded χ_loop, not a changed claim.
findings.evidence: Master l.401 (§3.5 minimal consciousness), l.256 (§3.3 active parts); docs/decisions.md l.828 (D-S366-J); findings F14, C07; crucible found no closure of either kind (C11).
findings.proposed_fix: After the χ_loop definition add: 'The parent theory distinguishes the active closure of the self and world models from a rudimentary closure that may hold among explicit content outside it (Gruber, 2026, Sections 3.3, 3.5); χ_loop should then be graded by closure strength rather than binary, with C(t) summing both grades and C_active(t) the active part alone.'

findings.quote: observational learning — extracting causal structure from watching another agent die — requires exactly the ESM-projection mechanism the formalization specifies (Section 5).
findings.problem: 'Requires' contradicts the paper's own prediction 1 and 2 framing two paragraphs later ('no architecture is asserted to be incapable of the task'; the claim is 'a price') and the crucible finding that the strongest reactive variant reached 0.45 and that a higher-capacity learner would likely close the gap. The transfer result (d = 2.44) is pre-conceded as not unique to FMT.
findings.evidence: docs/research/aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md Q10, Q40 (planner gap is capacity-relative); .claude/knowledge/prediction-framing.md item (4) 'not unique to FMT — pre-concede'; finding C20.
findings.proposed_fix: 'observational learning — extracting causal structure from watching another agent die — is the kind of task on which the ESM-projection mechanism the formalization specifies (Section 5) is predicted to pay, within a sample budget, over reactive architectures of matched capacity.'

reviewed.notes: Checks that came back clean: every in-text citation resolves to a reference-list entry and every listed entry is cited (66 entries, scripted cross-check); all formalization references are registry-verified in docs/aiw269-refs-verified.md and docs/reference-manifest.json (Wetterich 2022a is keyed 'Wetterich2022' there). The five-system hierarchy (§2.4), the §3.7.3 sufficiency conjunction (§4.5), the three principles (§1.1), the §6.0 'consequences not principles' pointer, the DID pointer to master §6.2, the 'computation is the thing being computed' quote (§3.4.3), the time-dilation attribution ('the parent paper does not state this prediction', confirmed absent from master) and the Oizumi semidirect-product attribution ('a prediction of this formalization', Oizumi absent from master) all match the master. Prediction 2 is aligned in substance (6e1961f0) apart from the dose-window/i_ext inconsistency in evidence-8. The §4.4 companion citation of the thirty-reservoir demand-gated peak is consistent with crucible's record. findings.section: §6.4 Self-Referential Closure as a Fixed Point (with §4.7, §5.1, §6.6)
findings.quote: Let m = (e, w) be the joint explicit state, with e the ESM state and w the EWM state, and define a map Ψ: M → M, Ψ(e, w) = ($h_{e}$(e, w), $h_{w}$(e, w)), in which each model's update takes the other as input. Self-referential closure occurs when: Ψ(m\*) = m\*
findings.problem: Ψ is defined on the joint explicit STATE, so Ψ(m*) = m* makes consciousness a stationary point of the state trajectory: at m* nothing changes, so experience would have no content change, the on-cluster complexity K of §4.7 (which must be high for consciousness) would be minimal, and §5.1's e(t), an input-driven attractor that moves with salient input, could never satisfy it. The master defines closure as the mutual UPDATING of the active self and world models, an ongoing process ('Their mutual updating is the closed loop'), and S342's PHENOMENAL-12 fix meant the fixed point of the coupled update rule, not of the state. The domain of Ψ is also inconsistent across the paper: M is the model space of §2.1, e is a scalar integral of ρ in §5.1, and §6.6 lets Ψ act on 'the space of effective theories at different scales'.
findings.evidence: Paper §6.4 l.495–505, §5.1 l.405–409 (e = integral of ρ), §4.7 l.375–379 (K); master §3.3 l.256 ('Their mutual updating is the closed loop, which gives the sense of being here and now'), master §3 Principle 3 l.137 ('each entering the other's update rule'); findings F11, C05; decisions.md:683 PHENOMENAL-12.
findings.proposed_fix: Define closure on the update rules, not the state: 'Let e_t, w_t be the active self- and world-model states (Gruber, 2026, §3.3) and h_e, h_w their update rules. Closure holds on a trajectory when w_t enters h_e and e_t enters h_w at every step: the pair of maps (h_e, h_w) is a fixed point of the representation relation (each model is represented in the other's rule), while the states e_t, w_t keep changing. Ψ denotes this coupled rule; Ψ(m*) = m* names the rule's self-consistency, not a stationary state.' Rename the joint state space (e.g. E × Wm) so M stays the model space of §2.1, and make e in §5.1 a state vector, not an integral of ρ.

findings.quote: ρ at the self-scope (s ≈ 0), explicit (ν > $\nu_{\mathrm{crit}}$) corner migrates toward the world-scope (s → 1) region while remaining above $\nu_{\mathrm{crit}}$. The system still runs an explicit simulation — consciousness is preserved
findings.problem: §2.3 requires, for any consciousness, mass above θ_ESM near the self-scope explicit corner, and says a system with mass only near (s = 1, ν = 1) 'would not be conscious'. §5.3 then moves that very mass to s → 1 and declares consciousness preserved. Either the §2.3 constraint is violated during ego dissolution, or the scope coordinate s does not mean 'content about the self' and the ESM corner must be defined by role (the model the senses are referred to), which the paper nowhere says. The master's minimal self model is 'a viewpoint projected into the world from which the senses seem to take their information', which is a role, not a content coordinate.
findings.evidence: Paper §2.3 l.90–96, §5.3 l.437; master §3.4.3 l.325 (viewpoint ≠ position estimate), §3.2 l.226 (redirected ESM 'latches onto whatever input is most salient'); findings F09, F10, F38.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the §5.3 sentence with: 'Redirection is a change of the ESM's input coupling (α → 0 in §5.1), not a migration of ρ out of the self-scope corner: the model that occupies the self role, the viewpoint to which the senses are referred (Gruber, 2026, §3.4.3), keeps its mass above θ_ESM while its content is sourced from world-scope input. In scope–mode terms, s indexes the role a model plays (self-locus vs. world), not what its current content is about, so the §2.3 constraint continues to hold under ego dissolution.' Then state the role reading of s once in §2.1.

findings.quote: At a fixed point of self-representation, there is no remainder — no "outside view" from which the process can be fully described without participating in it.
findings.problem: §6.4 states the no-outside property as a consequence of the fixed point, while §8 Phase 3 says the project is to 'Investigate whether the fixed-point condition can be shown to formally entail properties that correspond to the "no outside view" argument' and §9.1 says 'The fixed-point formalization either succeeds or fails'. The paper asserts in one section what it names as the open target in two others. Lawvere's theorem (and Kleene's recursion theorem, the same result read the other way) guarantees the EXISTENCE of self-reproducing fixed points and yields no inside/outside asymmetry by itself.
findings.evidence: Paper §6.4 l.501–503, §8 l.585, §9.1 l.623; finding F30 (No Outside §5.1, §7.1: Lawvere/Kleene give existence; 'self-reference on its own is constructive').
findings.proposed_fix: 'A fixed point of this kind exists by Lawvere's theorem (Lawvere, 1969; cf. Kauffman, 1987). Whether it entails the inside/outside asymmetry the parent theory identifies with experience (Gruber, 2026, §3.4.3) is the open question of Phase 3 (§8): existence of self-reproducing structure is proven, the no-outside property is the claim the formalization must deliver.' Delete the 'no remainder' sentence.

findings.section: §6.6 Self-Referential Closure as a Renormalization Group Fixed Point (vs §4.4, Abstract)
findings.quote: The self-referential closure condition Ψ(m\*) = m\* has precisely these properties: at the fixed point, the model and the modeled coincide (scale-invariance — the self-description is identical at every level of recursion), the system naturally evolves toward the fixed point (it is an attractor of the self-modeling dynamics), and only the relevant parameters of the self-model matter
findings.problem: Identifying closure with an RG fixed point (scale invariance, critical exponents, universality class, as §6.6 goes on to say) would make criticality a consequence of closure, which is exactly the chain the abstract says is 'neither a derived consequence of self-referential closure' and §4.4 declares open (L1, L2). §6.6 thus silently re-supplies the derivation §4.4 refuses. Two further defects: a critical RG fixed point is an attractor only on its critical surface and repulsive in its relevant directions, so 'the fixed point is an attractor of the RG flow, and only a finite number of relevant directions' misstates RG; and Wetterich's automaton–QFT equivalence is proven for reversible automata while cortical dynamics are dissipative, a precondition the companion cosmology itself has not checked.
findings.evidence: Paper Abstract l.15, §4.4 l.321–331, §6.6 l.517–525; master §3 l.137 Principle 1 (criticality is a signature, 'not the principle itself'); didactic-patterns.md 'Cautions' (criticality is a signature, free modelling the requirement); finding F43 (AIW-334 Wetterich residual, MG: track only).
findings.proposed_fix: Open §6.6 with the dependency stated: 'If closure were an RG fixed point, scale invariance and a universality class would follow, and with them the closure ⇒ criticality chain that §4.4 leaves open; the analogy therefore inherits L1 and L2 and is a Phase-3 target, not a result.' Correct the RG sentence to 'the fixed point attracts along its irrelevant directions and repels along its finitely many relevant ones'. Add to the Wetterich sentence: 'proven for globally reversible automata; whether it extends to dissipative dynamics such as cortex is unchecked (Gruber, 2026c, §8.4).'

findings.section: §7.2 The Consciousness Functor (vs §6.4 and master E11)
findings.quote: Consciousness is a **functor** F: Sub → Sim that maps substrate dynamics to simulation dynamics while preserving compositional structure
findings.problem: §7.2 locates consciousness in the substrate-to-simulation MAPPING. §6.4 locates phenomenal properties 'at m*', an object inside Sim. The master removed the mapping reading in S366: 'Consciousness arises within the explicit models this automaton carries, where the explicit self and world models update each other, while the structural knowledge base generates and sustains those models.' F is the generation relation the master assigns to the substrate, not consciousness.
findings.evidence: Paper §7.2 l.542–547, §6.4 l.505; master §3.3 l.297 (E11), Fig. 3 caption (E13: 'the closed loop of the explicit self and world models sets what does'); finding F17.
findings.proposed_fix: 'Generation is a functor F: Sub → Sim mapping substrate transitions to transitions of the explicit models. Consciousness is not F but a structure inside Sim: the closed loop in which the self-model and world-model objects enter each other's morphisms (§6.4). The real/virtual split is the distinction between Sub and Sim; the Hard Problem's category error is seeking in Sub a property of that Sim-internal structure.'

findings.quote: IWM = the world-knowledge partition of W. / ISM = the self-knowledge partition of W.
findings.problem: The abstract states scope is 'a nesting: ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM' and mode 'an orthogonal contrast'. §2.1 then makes scope a contrast axis identical in form to mode ('from pure self-representation (0) to pure world-representation (1)') with EWM at s = 1 as 'Pure world-simulation', and §4.1 makes IWM and ISM disjoint partitions of W. Both contradict the abstract and the master, where ISM ⊆ IWM is 2015-native and the closure partner is EWM ∖ ESM. The master also now says nesting is the normal mode with exceptions (disembodied salvinorin states, Cotard), which the abstract states unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Paper Abstract l.15, §2.1 l.57–67, §4.1 l.271–272; master §3.2 l.209 ('scope is a nesting ... Nesting is the normal mode of operation ... The part of the EWM outside the ESM ... is the world model with which the self model closes'), master §3.1 l.152 ('the self as a proper part of it'); findings F10, C06.
findings.proposed_fix: §2.1: 'The corner s = 1 is the explicit world model less the self model (EWM ∖ ESM), the partner the self model closes with; the nesting ESM ⊆ EWM is the statement that self-scope content is represented inside the same explicit frame as world-scope content, so s orders content from the self outward rather than contrasting two disjoint things.' §4.1: 'IWM = the world-knowledge of W; ISM = the self-knowledge within it (ISM ⊆ IWM).' Abstract: 'scope (a nesting in the normal mode of operation: ESM ⊆ EWM, ISM ⊆ IWM)'.

findings.quote: Any implementation of the model-space framework should include criteria for distinguishing real modes from artifacts — for example, requiring that identified modes correlate with behavior, stimulus content, or report, rather than treating every ICA component as a real model.
findings.problem: The paper never defines 'model' ('every point represents a distinct model the substrate is running') and its only reality criterion is correlation. The master now defines a model by write access (updates so that it follows its target, tested against a time-shifted null) and readability (the system can evaluate it; being read is required only for consciousness), with boundary recognition demoted to a consequence of the target domain. Crucible has shown the paper's criterion is insufficient: any rotation of a content-carrying subspace also correlates with behavior (8–9 of 18 random-basis directions 'counted' vs 2 for ICA), and the input area's rate must be the covariate.
findings.evidence: Paper §2.1 l.55, §2.6 l.140; master §3.1 l.152 and Table 1 l.164 ('A model must be readable; that it is actually read is required only for consciousness'); findings F01, F02, F03, C03, C13 (cru234-find-frozen §1–§4, cru227 §6).
findings.proposed_fix: §2.1, after 'a distinct model the substrate is running': 'A model here is a structure the system updates so that it follows a target domain (write access) and can evaluate (readability); that it is actually read is a condition on consciousness, not on model status (Gruber, 2026, §3.1, Table 1).' §2.6: 'requiring that an identified mode follows a target better than a time-shifted null with the input area's rate as covariate, that the test is rotation-invariant within the shared subspace or the basis is pre-stated, and that the mode's members project outside it (readability).'

findings.quote: σ < 1: subcritical (activity dies out) → Wolfram Class 1/2 ... $\lambda_{\max}$ < 0: ordered (stable attractors) ... $\lambda_{\max}$ > 0: chaotic
findings.problem: The two mappings disagree on measured cases: propofol is subcritical by branching (Class 1/2 under the σ map) and deeper into the chaotic phase by slow electrodynamics (Class 3 under the λ map), and waking cortex is slightly subcritical AND slightly chaotic (Toker et al., 2022, now in master Table 4). §4.5's 'deep propofol anesthesia, where cortical dynamics also turn subcritical' holds only on the branching axis; §4.3's 'states where the two measures diverge' are no longer hypothetical. The λ labels 'ordered' clash with Toker's terminology, in which the chaotic side is the 'ordered' phase for edge-of-chaos criticality. §8 Module 3 also says λ_max is 'already measured in the ConCrit literature', contradicting §4.3 ('ConCrit focuses primarily on the branching ratio') and omitting Toker 2022, the source that does measure it.
findings.evidence: Paper §4.2 l.287–297, §4.3 l.305, §4.5 l.339, §8 l.573; master Table 4 l.711–718 and column note ('The two axes move apart'), §5.3 l.720, §8.1 l.959; findings F19, F21 (D-S360-3), C17.
findings.proposed_fix: §4.2: drop the Wolfram-class labels from the σ list (keep sub-/critical/super-critical) and relabel λ as 'λ_max < 0: periodic / stable; ≈ 0: edge of chaos; > 0: chaotic / unstable'. Add after the band: 'The two axes move apart in measured states: waking cortex is slightly subcritical by branching (Priesemann et al., 2014) and slightly chaotic by its slow electrodynamics, propofol is subcritical by branching and deeper into chaos (Toker et al., 2022), so option 1 of §4.3 is already excluded as a joint requirement.' §4.5: 'turn subcritical on the branching axis'. §8 Module 3: 'σ is measured across the ConCrit literature and λ_max in Toker et al. (2022)'. Add Toker et al. 2022 to the references.

findings.quote: Compute transfer entropy between neural signals in known "implicit" processing regions and known "explicit"/"conscious access" regions
findings.problem: §3.1 defines permeability as T from A_s (implicit mass at scope s) to B_s (explicit mass at the same s), a split by mode at ν_crit, not by anatomy. §8 Module 2 and §9.1 ('Transfer entropy from implicit to explicit regions') operationalize it as TE between region pairs, which is a different quantity and invites the region misreading the master rules out (explicit models are activity, never regions). Table 1 also uses quantities §3.1 does not define: T_IWM→ESM is cross-scope, and 'T from parameters high' is undefined because W is static and TE needs two time series. Crucible adds that any lagged-prediction measure between two projections of one recurrent substrate is generically non-zero, so TE permeability needs a rotation null and conditioning on common input.
findings.evidence: Paper §3.1 l.166–172, §3.2 Table 1 l.188–191, §8 l.571, §9.1 l.617; master §3.2 l.209 ('not anatomically localized regions'); fmt-misconception-registry.md #5; findings C01, C12.
findings.proposed_fix: Module 2: 'Estimate A_s and B_s as the implicit and explicit modeling mass at each scope (§3.1; implicit from slow structural/parameter-tracking signals, explicit from running activity), compute T_{A_s→B_s} against a rotation null conditioned on common input, and test Table 1.' §9.1: 'implicit-to-explicit transfer entropy at scope s increases by factor k at dose d'. Table 1: replace 'T_ISM→ESM → 0; T_IWM→ESM ↑' with 'P(s≈0) → 0; I(e; i_ext) ↑ (§5.2)', and 'T from parameters high' with 'B_s sustained with sensory-input TE ≈ 0'.

findings.section: §3.5 Total Conscious Content and §6.3 levels table (vs master §3.5, §3.3, §3.6.1)
findings.quote: Let $\chi_{\mathrm{loop}}(s, \nu, t) \in [0, 1]$ be the fraction of the modeling activity at (s, ν) that is in the closed loop at time t.
findings.problem: χ_loop is a single in/out fraction and the §6.3 Minimal row reads 'Rudimentary closure; same depth as basic, poorer content'. The master (undeposited, MG-ruled, hedged 'can arise') now distinguishes the ACTIVE closure of the active self and world models (the sense of being here and now) from a rudimentary closure among NON-active explicit models that gives minimal consciousness, and identifies the active parts with the working model, the channel occupancy whose capacity 'is the rank of the channel'. The formalization cannot express two grades of closure, and C(t) carries no capacity bound, so it cannot state the master's §3.5 floor or the rank parameter the master calls a third dimension.
findings.evidence: Paper §3.5 l.251–253, §6.3 l.481; master §3.5 l.401 ('It can arise among non-active explicit models, without the active closure'), §3.3 l.256, §3.6.1 l.444–446, §3.7 ('A third dimension, and not a criticality one'); findings F11, F13, F14, F15, C07. Status: D-S366-J is a hedged hypothesis (MG 'may').
findings.proposed_fix: 'Let χ_act(s, ν, t) be the fraction of activity at (s, ν) in the active closed loop (the working model, Gruber, 2026, §3.6.1) and χ_rud the fraction in a rudimentary closure among non-active explicit models (Gruber, 2026, §3.5, stated there as a hypothesis); C(t) integrates χ_act, and minimal consciousness is C_act ≈ 0 with C_rud > 0. The active fraction is bounded by the channel's rank k: C_act(t) ≤ k, a capacity parameter independent of the two criticality dials of §4.7.' §6.3 Minimal row: 'Rudimentary closure among non-active explicit models; the self mirrored in the world model it closes with; same depth as basic, poorer content.'

findings.quote: The Meta-Problem becomes deductive. ... The observability constraint says this is architecturally impossible for self-referentially closed systems.
findings.problem: The constraint as formalized, O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM, bars direct reach-through to substrate processes, not a learned description of them: a neuroscientist's EWM can hold synapses as content, so 'complete access to its own substrate' in the sense the Hard Problem presupposes (a description) is not what the constraint forbids, and 'deductive' / 'architecturally impossible' claim more than the argument delivers. The master is more careful: the indexical-gap identity 'is not proven here' (§4.2.5), and the master's meta-problem has two mechanisms (universal opacity plus occasional leaks, §3.8), of which the formalization derives only the first.
findings.evidence: Paper §6.2 l.459–465; master §4.2.5 l.629 ('FMT needs the contrary claim ... and that claim is not proven here'), §3.8 (two mechanisms), §3.4.3 l.321 ('cannot see with useful resolution beyond'); findings F36, F37, F30 (No Outside: the limit is on the current act of generating, not on representing substrate facts as content).
findings.proposed_fix: 1. 'The Meta-Problem follows from the constraint: the processes generating the simulation are outside S_EWM as processes, so the ESM can hold a learned description of them but not represent its own generation as it occurs; the felt opacity is this structural gap, and the parent theory adds a second, leak-based mechanism (Gruber, 2026, §3.8) that the diffusion term D of §3.4 can carry.' 2. 'The Hard Problem's formulation asks for experience to appear in an outside description. The constraint says the ESM cannot occupy that description of its own generation from inside; that this indexical gap is the phenomenal gap is the parent theory's claim, stated there as unproven (Gruber, 2026, §4.2.5), and it is what §6.4 and Phase 3 must deliver.'

findings.quote: (3) criticality as a signature hypothesis (empirically motivated, resting on two open lemmas, and neither a derived consequence of self-referential closure nor a stated requirement on consciousness)
findings.problem: The signature hypothesis does not rest on the lemmas; the DERIVATION of criticality from closure does. §4.4 says the signature 'stand[s] entirely on their own as empirical instruments, independent of whether L1 and L2 are ever closed', and §1.3 states it correctly ('whose derivation from self-referential closure rests on two open lemmas'). The abstract contradicts both.
findings.evidence: Paper Abstract l.15, §1.3 l.47, §4.4 l.331.
findings.proposed_fix: '(3) criticality as a signature hypothesis, empirically motivated and a stated requirement on nothing, whose derivation from self-referential closure rests on two open lemmas'.

findings.quote: This argument needs formal grounding. Three mathematical approaches are proposed:
findings.problem: §6.2 (observability), §6.3 (recursive depth), §6.4 (fixed point) and §6.6 ('A fourth approach ... from an unexpected direction') make four; §6.5 is a cost bound, not an approach. The count announced in §6.1 does not match the section.
findings.proposed_fix: 'Four mathematical approaches are proposed (§6.2–6.4, §6.6); §6.5 bounds their cost.'

findings.quote: P∞ makes the binding claim of §5.1 (maximal correlation length ⇒ substrate-spanning integration) the *same quantity* as extent
findings.problem: §5.1 of this paper is 'The ESM as an Input-Dependent Attractor' and contains no binding claim. The binding claim is the parent paper's §5.1 ('Binding as an Emergent Property of the Substrate's Dynamics'), which §2.5 cites correctly as 'Section 5.1 of the parent paper'.
findings.proposed_fix: 'the binding claim of the parent paper (Gruber, 2026, §5.1: maximal correlation length ⇒ substrate-spanning integration)'.

findings.quote: The *route* out is phase- and scale-dependent and is not settled — onset and spread are heterogeneous and often desynchronized at single-neuron scale, while hypersynchrony dominates the late phase and termination — so the case should be stated route-agnostically as exit from Class 4
findings.problem: The master now carries direct human evidence that generalized seizures cross the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022; two intracranial, one MEG), the hypersynchrony route, while focal recordings lose power-law statistics (Meisel et al., 2012). 'Not settled' is stale for generalized seizures; the route-robust invariant can stay, but the paper should not understate the evidence the master cites. didactic-patterns.md's 'Cautions' seizure item (S300) is partly superseded the same way.
findings.evidence: Paper §4.7 l.381; master §3.7 l.501 ('Direct human evidence for that departure exists for both seizure types'), §10.3 l.1158; finding F20 (AIW-340, n = 3).
findings.proposed_fix: 'The route out differs by seizure type and phase: in the generalized seizures measured so far (n = 3) the slow electrodynamics cross the edge of chaos into the periodic phase (Toker et al., 2022), focal onset is heterogeneous at single-neuron scale (Truccolo et al., 2011), and hypersynchrony dominates late phase and termination; the decomposition needs only that Class 4 is exited, so E ≈ 0 holds on every route.'

findings.section: §4.5 The Two Thresholds as a Conjunction
findings.quote: That the architecture entails free modeling would be Lemma L1 of §4.4, which is open.
findings.problem: L1 as stated in §4.4 is 'closure ⇒ universality'. Its antecedent is closure, not the four-corner architecture of §4.5 (which does not include closure), and its consequent is Turing universality, which §4.4 itself distinguishes from free modeling and from approximation universality. The gloss misidentifies the lemma.
findings.evidence: Paper §4.4 l.327 ('Lemma L1 (closure ⇒ universality)'), l.329 ('approximation universality is not computational (Turing) universality'), §4.5 l.341.
findings.proposed_fix: 'That closure entails open-ended computation is close to Lemma L1 of §4.4 (closure ⇒ universality), which is open, and the architecture condition here does not include closure; until a lemma of that shape is proven the two thresholds are stated as co-required but logically independent.'

findings.quote: the additional layers provide the overhead needed for recursive self-simulation (Gruber, 2015). Recurrence can substitute running time for depth: a single ReLU recurrent network with fixed weights and fixed hidden dimension uniformly approximates every continuous function on [−1, 1] if run long enough
findings.problem: The Abadie et al. sentence undercuts the layer argument it follows without reconciliation: if recurrence substitutes time for depth, extra cortical layers are not needed for recursion overhead, only time is. The paragraph leaves the two claims side by side. The master's new running-cost claim (the closed loop 'like any virtual machine is slower than the hardware beneath it') gives the reconciliation: the overhead is paid in depth or in time, and the formalization's cost bound counts only capacity.
findings.evidence: Paper §6.5 l.513; master §4.2.4 l.623 (VM tax; 'capability scales with the internal simulation budget ... and stops scaling when closure is ablated'); finding F26.
findings.proposed_fix: 'The overhead can be paid in depth or in running time: a fixed-width recurrent network approximates any continuous function if run long enough, with the runtime unavoidable (Abadie et al., 2026), so the bound above has a dual in latency. The parent theory predicts the time cost: on long-horizon tasks capability scales with the simulation budget when closure is in place and stops scaling when it is ablated (Gruber, 2026, §4.2.4), a formalizable Phase 4 prediction (§8).'

findings.section: §3.3 The Selection Operator as a Family of Mechanisms
findings.quote: Define a **selection family** $G = \{g_c : W \times X \to [0, 1]^{N_c}\}$, indexed by channel c ∈ C ... and $N_c$ is the dimensionality of channel c's spatial resolution ... The composite selection state is the element-wise product across channels: g(W, x(t)) = \prod_{c \in C} g_c(W, x(t))
findings.problem: An element-wise product across channels with channel-specific dimensions N_c is undefined, and the product g ⊙ W then multiplies a vector by the N × N matrix W. The dimensions never match as written.
findings.proposed_fix: 'g_c : W × X → [0, 1]^{N×N}, each channel a mask on the couplings of W at its own spatial resolution (a coarser channel assigns one value to every coupling inside a parcel), so the element-wise product and g ⊙ W are defined on the same index set.'

findings.quote: Permeability asks how much of what happens below the threshold of consciousness shows up, a moment later, in what happens above it.
findings.problem: ν_crit is the implicit–explicit threshold; §2.2 and §3.5 say explicit content is conscious only where it enters the closed loop. Calling ν_crit 'the threshold of consciousness' contradicts both.
findings.proposed_fix: 'below the implicit–explicit threshold'.

findings.quote: above $\nu_{\mathrm{crit}}$, it is low-dimensional, structured, and local (explicit)
findings.problem: 'local' explicit processing reads as spatial localization, the misreading the master rules out (explicit models are activity, never regions), and sits against §4.7, where conscious processing needs a substrate-spanning giant critical cluster. §1.2 ('four *regions* in a continuous space') and §2.3 ('four regions R_IWM ...') use 'region' for corners of an abstract space; the RCA records that the word invites the region reading.
findings.evidence: Paper §1.2 l.41, §2.3 l.92, §4.6 l.351, §4.7 l.373; docs/research/fmt-crucible-misread-rca.md §2; finding F05; fmt-misconception-registry.md #5.
findings.proposed_fix: §4.6: 'low-dimensional and structured, with local structure in the graph-theoretic sense (short characteristic paths, high clustering), not confined to a region of tissue'. §1.2/§2.3: 'four *corners* of a continuous space' and 'four neighborhoods R_k of the corners'.

findings.quote: the spectral radius tunes the substrate's open-ended computational *capability*, and the edge is not where that capability peaks (Section 4.4)
findings.problem: The crucible record behind this (CRU-203, cited in §4.4 via Gruber 2026d) measured only shallow, memory-bound tasks (a lag-6 operand-memory peak in rate reservoirs); no open-ended capability was measured, so locating open-ended capability away from the edge overstates it. The same paragraph's 'Computational validation is reported in the companion (Gruber, 2026d)' points at a companion whose §6 calls an at-risk, un-rerun null 'clean', reads A#6 as closure maintenance, and rests §5 on region-labelled ClosureBrain, all now out of line with crucible's record (AIW-361, companion v7 pending).
findings.evidence: Paper §8 l.589, l.595; docs/research/aiw130-s6-crucible-check-s365.md Q19 ('No open-ended capability was measured in any rate reservoir'); findings C19, F23, F24, C18.
findings.proposed_fix: 'the spectral radius tunes the substrate's computational regime; on the shallow memory-bound tasks measured so far the accuracy peak lies in the driven-stable regime, not at the edge (Section 4.4), and no open-ended task has been measured'. Replace 'Computational validation is reported in the companion' with 'The companion (Gruber, 2026d) reports the in-silico tests to date; the specification below does not depend on them', and hold the deposit until companion v7 matches crucible's record (AIW-361).

findings.section: §8 Module 4, Phase 4 ablations, §5.2 (ESM as a unit)
findings.quote: Build a minimal computational model with a self-model unit and demonstrate input-dependent identity switching under perturbation.
findings.problem: 'self-model unit', 'FMT-minus-ESM', 'ESM ablation' and 'default mode network activity (proxy for ESM)' (§5.2) all treat the ESM as a removable part or a region, against the paper's own §4.1 (explicit models are 'patterns of activity') and the master's ruling that explicit models are emergent activity, never a module; crucible's gridworld transfer result uses a module-ESM agent whose status under that ruling is an open question. The ablation-validity audit already requires proof of removal; it should also say what is removed when the ESM is activity.
findings.proposed_fix: Module 4: 'Build a minimal recurrent model in which a self-model direction emerges in the activity, identify it by the §2.6 criteria, and demonstrate ...'. Phase 4: 'FMT-minus-ESM (the self-model direction suppressed by efferent disconnection or targeted perturbation, with its removal verified by the audit below)'. §5.2: 'activity in self-referential networks (a neural correlate of the ESM, not a localization; Gruber, 2026, Table 1 note c)'.

findings.quote: | Salvia divinorum (high dose) | High + ESM disruption | Self-scope P collapses | $T_{\mathrm{ISM} \to \mathrm{ESM}} \to 0$; $T_{\mathrm{IWM} \to \mathrm{ESM}}$ ↑ |
findings.problem: §5.2 and the master's Prediction 2 run the controllability tests below the gating dose, because at the highest doses external audiovisual input is gated and identity content is predicted to come from internal imagery. A row labelled 'high dose' predicting uptake of world content does not say which dose range it means, and the master names a window (Maqueda et al., 2015).
findings.evidence: Paper §3.2 l.188, §5.2 l.429; master §8.3 l.987ff. ('the tests run at doses below the gating range'); finding F38.
findings.proposed_fix: 'Salvia divinorum (ego-dissolving dose below the external-input gating range; Gruber, 2026, §8.3)' with the measurement column aligned to §5.2 (I(e; i_self) → 0; I(e; i_ext) ↑), and a second row 'highest dose: external input gated; identity content internally sourced'.

findings.quote: The formalization predicts that the closed-loop quantity C(t) should correlate with PCI and similar complexity measures across consciousness states.
findings.problem: §4.7 says PCI and LZc 'map onto K, **not** onto extent' and that C(t) 'is a joint quantity (it rises when either dial rises)'. A reader is told PCI tracks C(t) in §3.5 and tracks only the K component of it in §4.7; the two statements need the relation stated once.
findings.proposed_fix: 'C(t) should co-vary with PCI across states through its complexity component (§4.7, K); a state with high extent and low on-cluster complexity would separate the two.'

findings.quote: the EWM is the active representation (the encoder's output)
findings.problem: The master now reserves 'active' for the part of a model inside the closed loop (active world model / active self model) and renames other uses 'running'. The paper uses 'active' in the old sense here, in §6.2 ('the EWM actively models') and in §7.4 ('with only one active at any given time'), which will collide with the master's terminology once the formalization adopts the active/non-active partition (coherence-10).
findings.evidence: Paper §2.5 l.124, §6.2 l.455, §7.4 l.561; master §3.3 l.256, Table 4 ('All four running'); finding F11 (T3).
findings.proposed_fix: 'the EWM is the running representation'; 'that the EWM currently models'; 'with only one running at any given time'.

findings.quote: $\mu_{n}$: $X_{\mathrm{ESM}}$ → M($X_{\mathrm{ESM}}$^(n-1)) ... | Basic consciousness | μ₀ | ESM represents the EWM |
findings.problem: At n = 0 the codomain M(X_ESM^(−1)) is undefined, yet the table's μ₀ is 'ESM represents the EWM', whose codomain is models of X_EWM, not of X_ESM. The recursion needs a base case.
findings.proposed_fix: 'μ₀: X_ESM → M(X_EWM) (the ESM represents the world model); μ_n: X_ESM → M(im μ_{n−1}) for n ≥ 1 (the ESM represents its own previous-level representation).'

findings.quote: Phase 2 now includes the category-theoretic architecture alongside the model-space and ESM modules, reflecting the recognition that the categorical framework is not an optional formalism but the canonical mathematical language for emergence from discrete substrates.
findings.problem: Narrates the document's own revision history ('now includes', 'reflecting the recognition') and carries a not-X-but-Y for rhythm; the sentence says the same thing with the pairing removed.
findings.evidence: prose-register.md, 'Narrating the document's own revision history' and 'Cadence tics'.
findings.proposed_fix: 'Phase 2 places the category-theoretic architecture beside the model-space and ESM modules, because the categorical framework should shape their construction rather than be fitted to them afterwards.'

findings.quote: It should be attributed carefully: the parent paper does not state this prediction ... This time-dilation *law* is roadmap-grade, not main-paper-grade; the main paper does not state it.
findings.problem: The same fence stated twice in one subsection, the second time with grade labels that stage the paper's own positioning ('roadmap-grade', 'main-paper-grade').
findings.evidence: Paper l.389 and l.393; prose-register.md 'Structural slop: Fencing' and 'Narrating the paper's own rhetorical strategy'.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep one clause at the opening: 'The parent paper treats subjective time through its temporal-echo mechanism (Gruber, 2026, Section 3.4.4) and does not state this prediction; it is developed here.' Delete the closing sentence.

findings.quote: This subsection gives the decomposition a formal basis by abandoning the single-point picture, and locates the two dials on genuinely distinct mathematical objects. The construction below is offered as the recommended formalization, not as a derived result ... This is a real departure from §4.2
findings.problem: A cluster of self-narration: the subject of three sentences is the subsection, its construction and its relation to §4.2, with 'genuinely' and 'real' as value-words.
findings.evidence: prose-register.md 'Self-narration of the document's own moves'; 'Empty value-words'.
findings.proposed_fix: 'Replacing the single critical point with a field of locally critical regions puts the two dials on distinct mathematical objects; the independence of the dials is a conjecture (item 4).' Cut 'This is a real departure from §4.2' and open the paragraph with 'In §4.2, σ and α are whole-recording estimates; here they are estimated per region ...'.

findings.quote: If these predictions hold, they demonstrate that the formalized framework's mathematical structure captures genuine computational distinctions. If they fail, they identify which formal commitments are wrong. Either outcome advances the theory.
findings.problem: Canned aphorism dressed as insight, plus a lecture on how science works ('Either outcome advances the theory'), with 'genuine' as filler.
findings.evidence: prose-register.md 'Cadence tics' and 'Lecturing the reader on scientific method'.
findings.proposed_fix: 'If these predictions hold, the formal structure captures computational distinctions; if they fail, they name the formal commitment that is wrong.' Delete the third sentence.

findings.quote: reuses the graph-phase-transition machinery already introduced in §4.6 (clustering, modularity, giant component) with little new apparatus — the single cheapest formal win. ... integration and extent are one order parameter, not two ideas.
findings.problem: 'the single cheapest formal win' is an empty superlative/value-phrase; 'one order parameter, not two ideas' is a not-X-but-Y for rhythm. Both sentences survive unchanged without the tails.
findings.evidence: prose-register.md 'Empty superlative dressed as insight', 'Cadence tics'.
findings.proposed_fix: 'and reuses the graph machinery of §4.6 (clustering, modularity, giant component).' ... 'P∞ makes the parent paper's binding claim the same quantity as extent.'

findings.quote: Notation alone does not make a theory testable. Φ is a fully specified mathematical object that has never been computed for a real brain and is provably intractable for realistic systems (Aaronson, 2014). Testability comes from **accepting constraints**
findings.problem: Two sentences whose subject is how testability works in general, the banned 'lecturing on scientific method' class; the Φ example carries the point on its own.
findings.evidence: prose-register.md 'Lecturing the reader on scientific method or epistemology'.

By that standard FMT's gap is specific: ...'

verdicts.reason: Defect real: §6.4 l.495 introduces Ψ on 'the joint explicit state' with temporal updates h_e, h_w, so Ψ(m*)=m* literally names a stationary state, which conflicts with §5.1 (input-driven attractor), §4.7 (K must be high on the cluster) and master Principle 3 / §3.3 l.256 ('Their mutual updating is the closed loop'); the domain is also inconsistent (M is the model space of §2.1, §6.3 uses M(·) as an operator, §6.6 lets Ψ act on 'effective theories'). But the evidence misreads the record: the S342 PHENOMENAL-12 fix itself said 'Define Ψ on the joint state (e, w) as the coupled update, with closure as its fixed point' (docs/reviews/2026-10-19-corpus-crosscheck.md l.556-559), so the state wording is what S342 asked for, not a drift from it. The proposed replacement ('the pair of maps (h_e, h_w) is a fixed point of the representation relation') is not a defined mathematical object. Severity is major, not critical: the paper already calls Ψ 'a map between models'.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Keep Ψ as a map on representational content (the model space of §2.1), not on activity states, and define closure as an invariant set of the coupled update: a set A with Ψ(A) = A on which each model's content includes the other's current content, while the trajectory keeps moving inside A with input. State in one sentence that the fixed point is of the representation relation at every step, not of the state trajectory. Rename the joint state space (E × Wm) and the §6.3 'models of' operator (Mod(·)) so M stays the model space; make e in §5.1 a state vector rather than an integral of ρ.

verdicts.reason: Defect real: §2.3 l.90-96 requires mass above θ_ESM in R_ESM for any consciousness; §5.3 l.437 moves that mass to s → 1 and declares consciousness preserved; and §5.1 l.405 defines e(t) as the integral over that same region, so under §5.3 e → 0 while §5.1 says the ESM persists with new content. Master §3.4.3 l.325 (viewpoint = origin to which the senses are referred, a role) and §3.2 l.226 (redirected ESM 'latches onto whatever input is most salient') support the role reading of the self model. The fix overreaches: making s 'index the role a model plays' in §2.1 breaks §2.1's own blended-content axis (the reaching model at intermediate s) and §3.1's scope-resolved permeability, which both need s to be target content.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Keep s as target/content scope. In §2.3 add: 'R_ESM is defined by the role a model plays in the closure, the viewpoint to which the senses are referred and which closes with the world model (Gruber, 2026, §3.4.3), not by its s-coordinate alone.' Rewrite §5.3: 'Redirection is a change of the ESM's input coupling (α → 0, §5.1) and of the content the self-role model carries; its mass in R_ESM stays above θ_ESM while its content is sourced from world-scope input, so the §2.3 constraint holds. Where the self model has nothing to latch onto (disembodied dissolution under salvinorin A; Gruber, 2026, §3.2) nesting itself may fail and R_ESM mass may fall; the formalization then predicts degraded rather than preserved consciousness.' Align §5.1's e(t) with the role reading.

verdicts.reason: Defect confirmed: §6.4 l.503 asserts 'no remainder — no outside view' as a consequence of the fixed point while §8 l.585 and §9.1 l.623 name that entailment as the open Phase 3 target; No Outside §5.1 (l.297-320) states that Lawvere/Kleene give existence ('Self-reference on its own is constructive') and no inside/outside asymmetry.
