missed.section: §3.1 Transfer Entropy Formulation vs §4.1 The Substrate as a Dynamical System
missed.quote: The implicit models are the *parameters* of this system: - IWM = the world-knowledge partition of W. - ISM = the self-knowledge partition of W.
missed.problem: §3.1 needs A_s(t), the implicit modeling mass at scope s, as a time series that carries information to the explicit mass B_s(t); §4.1 makes the implicit models the static parameters W and assigns no activity to the implicit side (x(t) is only projected onto the explicit models), so the paper's highest-priority quantity T_{A_s→B_s} has a source signal the paper never locates in its own dynamical system. Read literally with §4.1, A_s is constant and the transfer entropy is zero by construction. The master places implicit modeling in substrate processing, not in the weights alone.
missed.evidence: Paper §3.1 l.166-172, §4.1 l.269-279; master §3.1 l.152 ('stored in connectivity and evaluated by substrate processing'), Table 1 'Implicit model' row l.164-170.
missed.proposed_fix: §4.1: 'The implicit models are W together with the substrate processing W governs: the components of x(t) outside the explicit projections (the orthogonal complement of the ranges of Π_EWM and Π_ESM) are implicit modeling activity, A_s(t) of §3.1 is their mass at scope s, and W is their slow parameter. W itself carries no time series; permeability is estimated from that activity, not from the weights.'

missed.section: §3.3 The Selection Operator vs §3.1 Transfer Entropy Formulation
missed.quote: A single scalar "permeability" P emerges as a summary statistic — for example, the mean of g over spatial dimensions — but the fundamental quantity is the channel-indexed family.
missed.problem: Permeability P is defined twice, incompatibly, and the two definitions are never related: §3.1 defines P(s, t) as transfer entropy between implicit and explicit activity, §3.3 defines P as the spatial mean of a mask g on the coupling matrix W. One is an observable on activity, the other a parameter of the substrate dynamics; a reader cannot tell which quantity Table 1 predicts or which §9.1 calls falsifiable.
missed.proposed_fix: §3.3: 'The selection family g is the mechanism and T_{A_s→B_s} (§3.1) the observable; the symbol P is reserved for the latter. The formalization's commitment is a monotone functional form T_{A_s→B_s} = φ(ḡ_s), with ḡ_s the mean of g over the couplings serving scope s, to be fitted on dose–response data; a non-monotone relation absent a ceiling effect refutes it (Gruber, 2026, §3.6).'

missed.quote: Attention directs drift along ν (making implicit content explicit); context shifts direct drift along s
missed.problem: The Fokker-Planck picture transports modeling mass across ν_crit: implicit content becomes explicit by drift of the same density, and propofol gets 'an absorbing boundary at ν_crit'. §6.2 l.459 and the master say the opposite: the explicit models are generated from the substrate, not filled by a copy of it, and permeability names how readily substrate knowledge is drawn into that generation. §3.1's transfer-entropy reading (implicit activity predicting explicit activity) is the generation reading; §3.4 is the transport reading. The two are not reconciled, and one of the paper's three named 'constraints' (§9.1) is the transport one.
missed.evidence: Paper §3.4 l.230-243, §6.2 l.459 ('generated from the substrate, not filled by a copy of it'), §3.1 l.166-172, §9.1 l.615; master §3.6 l.417 ('The explicit models are generated from the substrate, not filled by a copy of it; permeability names how readily substrate-level knowledge or self-knowledge is drawn into that generation').
missed.proposed_fix: Recast v_ν as a recruitment rate, not a transport velocity: the source term S above ν_crit is proportional to the implicit mass A_s and the selection state g at that scope, S(s, ν > ν_crit, t) = κ(g) A_s(t), with no mass leaving the region below ν_crit; drift v acts only within each side (along s, and along ν within the implicit depth). Propofol is then κ → 0 (generation stops) rather than an absorbing boundary, and the Fokker-Planck form becomes consistent with §6.2 and §3.1.

missed.section: §4.2 Three Candidate Criticality Measures (definition of free modeling)
missed.quote: The theory requires free modeling — open-ended (Wolfram Class 4; Wolfram, 2002) computational capability recruited for self-modeling
missed.problem: Free modeling is defined by the regime label (Class 4), which identifies the requirement with the signature. The master states that 'the capability is not confined there ... The requirement is the capability, not the regime label', and the paper's own §4.4 treats Class-4 dynamics as the open consequent of L2, not as the definition of the antecedent. The same identification recurs in §4.5 l.339 and §4.7 l.357-381 ('Class-4 regime', 'exit from Class 4').
missed.evidence: Paper §4.2 l.283, §4.4 l.321-331, §4.5 l.339, §4.7 l.357, l.381; master §3.7.3 l.531 ('universal computation is proved for engineered networks that carry no criticality condition ... The requirement is the capability, not the regime label'); didactic-patterns.md Cautions (criticality a signature, free modelling the requirement).
missed.proposed_fix: §4.2: 'free modeling — open-ended computational capability, of the kind Wolfram's Class 4 automata exhibit but not confined to them (Gruber, 2026, §3.7.3), recruited for self-modeling'. In §4.7 write 'near-critical (Class-4-like) dynamics' where the regional indicator c_i is meant, so the indicator is a signature estimate and not the requirement.

missed.quote: **Self-referential loop**: ESM models the system generating the ESM (recursive depth ≥ 2)
missed.problem: The Phase 4 agent is specified at recursion depth ≥ 2, which in the paper's own §6.3 table is doubly extended consciousness (μ₂, reflection), while closure, the property the ablations test, is already present at μ₀ (minimal and basic). The test agent is therefore built to a stronger condition than Principle 3 requires, and a null on closure cannot be separated from a null on depth.
missed.evidence: Paper §8 l.597, §6.3 l.479-485 (μ₀ 'Rudimentary closure' / 'ESM represents the EWM', μ₂ doubly extended); master §3.5 l.401-409 (closure at the floor, reflection at the doubly extended rung).
missed.proposed_fix: '**Self-referential loop**: the self-model and world-model enter each other's update (closure at depth μ₀, §6.3); deeper rungs (μ₁, μ₂) are optional arms that test recursion depth separately from closure.'

missed.section: §6.2 The Observability Constraint vs the master's nesting exceptions
missed.quote: introduces an **observability constraint** that is architecturally constitutive, not merely epistemic: the ESM's observational horizon is bounded by the EWM.
missed.problem: O_ESM ⊆ S_EWM is stated without exceptions. If it is the nesting ESM ⊆ EWM in another notation (the ESM's representable content lies inside the explicit world model), it inherits the master's new ruling that nesting is the normal mode and can fail (disembodied dissolution under salvinorin A, Cotard's delusion); if it is a distinct horizon claim (the ESM cannot represent the substrate that generates it, regardless of nesting), the paper should say so, because §5.1's α → 0 case is exactly where the master lets nesting fail. The paper does not distinguish the two inclusions.
missed.evidence: Paper §6.2 l.453-459, §5.1 l.411-415; master §3.2 l.209 (HEAD: 'Nesting is the normal mode of operation ... It can fail when the self model has nothing to latch onto'), §3.4.3 l.321 (horizon constraint, unqualified); decisions.md D-S366-F.
missed.proposed_fix: After the constraint: 'This is a horizon claim, distinct from the content nesting ESM ⊆ EWM of §2.1: the nesting can fail when the self model has nothing to latch onto (Gruber, 2026, §3.2), the horizon cannot, because what the ESM represents is in every case drawn from the explicit simulation rather than from the substrate directly. Under the redirection of §5.1 the horizon holds while the nesting may not.'
